text: Appliance electrification

Community garden projects (must benefit whole housing community); measures delaying stormwater runoff; circular-economy projects (e.g. reused materials); planning/pre-feasibility studies; participatory planning processes within housing communities; and (via Grätzlmarie) repair cafés, community-room design, neighbourhood festivals

Supported practices beyond the core measures include: biodiverse greening of lawn/bare soil (Biodivers vergroenen van gazon en/of blote aarde, €15/m²); green roof stability/feasibility study (Stabiliteitsonderzoek groendak, €250 for single-family homes / €500 for apartment buildings >150m² roof); and on-site infiltration devices such as wadis or sunken planting beds (infiltratie via wadi's of verlaagde plantenvakken)
High-ecological-value planting (Categorie 2)
Tegeltuin (pavement/tile garden greening of street-facing strips); tree-pit adoption (boomtuintje); subsidised home visit advice from 'groene huisdokter' covering all greening options for the home

Yes -- infiltration facilities, rainwater use, and greening of front gardens are named as covered practices under the same municipal subsidy regulation as the green roof premium, but detailed terms/amounts for these sub-measures are not given in the fetched text
Solar photovoltaic system (energy); solar water heating; residual/greywater reuse; habite-se (occupancy permit) status noted by news source as scoring 1 pt

Reuso de água (water reuse system); aquecimento solar hidráulico (solar water heating); geração de energia solar fotovoltaica (photovoltaic solar power generation); uso de materiais sustentáveis na construção (use of sustainable construction materials); manutenção de área permeável com vegetação (maintenance of a permeable vegetated area)

Uso de energia solar (solar energy use); coleta seletiva (selective/source-separated waste collection); construção com materiais sustentáveis (construction with sustainable materials); manutenção de áreas verdes (maintenance of green areas)

Solar water heating; photovoltaic electricity; passive-energy design; wind energy; sustainable construction materials; native-tree cultivation and invasive-species control on undeveloped lots; solid-waste separation in condominiums/buildings; ecological sewage treatment where municipal sewerage is unavailable

Sistema de Reuso de Água (water reuse system); Sistema de Aquecimento Hidráulico Solar (solar water heating system); Sistema de Aquecimento Elétrico Solar (solar electric heating system); Construções com Material Sustentável (sustainable building materials); Utilização de Energia Passiva (passive energy use); Sistema de Utilização de Energia Eólica (wind energy system); Sistema de Energia Solar Fotovoltaica (photovoltaic solar energy); Preservação de Vegetação Nativa em Imóvel Não Edificado/Terrenos (native vegetation preservation on vacant lots); Plano de Gerenciamento de Resíduos (waste management plan)
Water reuse; solar water heating; certified sustainable construction materials; photovoltaic electricity generation
Bidet; water-saving faucet; low-flow toilet; drip/porous garden hose; low-flow showerhead; other WaterSense-certified products
Composters (backyard composting bins) sold at subsidised residential price alongside rain barrels; no other NbS practices documented.

Backyard composters (subsidised sale, $25 plus tax, with free kitchen catcher); rain barrels and electronic water timers ($55 plus tax) for efficient irrigation; water-wise/xeriscape gardening advice and workshops (Waterwise Gardening); toilet replacement rebate for water efficiency; leak repair guidance
Clover seed; manual or electric lawnmowers; reusable hygiene products; conventional/electric bicycles; child trailers and trailer bicycles

Downspout disconnections; Rain barrels/storage tanks; Rain gardens/box planters; Soakaway pits; Permeable pavement; Absorbent landscaping (MF/ICI only); Soil cells (MF/ICI only); Backwater valve subsidy (separate existing programme, SF only, excluded from RainWise cap)

Backwater valves (sewer backflow prevention), sump pit/pump installation, eavestrough (downspout) extenders, and sanitary lateral lining -- all targeted at reducing inflow/infiltration (I&I) and basement flooding risk.

Qualified Stormwater Best Management Practices that detain peak flow on an ongoing basis (unspecified generic category); specific practices not itemized in this Regulations document -- reserved to the Commission's Stormwater Credit Manual
Soakaway pits; dry wells; infiltration trenches; enhanced grass swales; perforated-pipe systems; downspout redirection/disconnection; comprehensive multi-feature LID plans; native planting

Replacement of cool-season turf; climate-appropriate plants; drought-tolerant turf; sufficient growing medium; mulch and soil amendments; irrigation-controller upgrades; flow sensors; pressure regulation; efficient sprinklers; micro-irrigation

Infiltration galleries (residential); for non-residential properties: filter strips, paved area sweeping programs, salt management programs (quality credit); combination BMPs directing impervious area to management practice (quantity credit); employee/public/student education programs (education credit); Rain Smart Neighbourhoods Project offers free consultations for yard projects including tree planting and rain gardens (separate from the fee credit program)

Native/pollinator biodiversity garden creation: front-yard or side-yard "jardin en façade" garden (min. 9 m², ≥36 plants/shrubs, ≥25% native species incl. at least one of agastache/asclepias/heliopsis/monarda/solidago, ≥5 species, ≥80% perennials) OR riverside/riparian buffer "jardin en rive" garden within 15m of a watercourse (min. 15 m², ≥60 plants, 100% native and perennial, ≥15% shrubs); eligible materials include compost, manure, mycorrhizae, uncoloured mulch/wood chips, ramial chipped wood, geotextile/geomembrane, and insect hotel construction/purchase materials.
Low-flow toilet replacement (water-efficiency retrofit, not a green-infrastructure/NbS measure)
Community gardens; aquaponics; ecological landscaping; native and wildlife-supporting planting; habitat corridors; lighting/appliance efficiency; renewable ener

Subsidised sale of composters and rain barrels; distribution of free trees, assorted "trousses" (kits) and compost; educational guided visit of the wastewater treatment plant (Centre d'épuration des eaux/CERS) -- all offered as part of the annual "Journée verte" event

Xeriscaping/drought-tolerant landscaping practices (organic mulches, landscape rock mixes, eco-friendly artificial turf from renewable/recyclable materials, native grass seed mixes, non-turf grass ground-cover such as white/micro clover, landscape fabric weed barriers); home composting units; drip irrigation systems/low-flow heads; smart irrigation controllers with soil-moisture/weather-based sensors
Detention basins, ponds, underground chambers, inlet controls, oil/grit separators, infiltration, sustainable landscaping, sweeping, salt and pollution-prevention plans

Green roofing/vegetated roof installation ($100/m², Blocks 1-3); replacing paved/asphalt surfaces with vegetated surface or grass pavers ($1,700/building, Blocks 1-3); French drain (foundation drain) installation/replacement ($60/linear metre, Blocks 1-3); roof-drain diversion/downspout redirection ($3,750/building); plus flood-resilience measures (sump pump, check valves, backflow valves, watertight doors, metal flood barriers, garage entrance infill, driveway raising) under Blocks 1-3; secondary building demolition (Block 2, $2,000/building)
Rainwater collection system components (transport piping, debris traps, filters, installation costs); no other NbS practices supported
Drought-tolerant native planting; manual watering; sprinkler checks [advice only]; rain-barrel watering exemption
Cool roofs (new membrane or coating over an existing roof)
bioswales, infiltration galleries, downspout redirection and professional designs -- no value change proposed on S4 alone
Downspout disconnection (directing existing downspout to rain garden area) as an integral design requirement
Native shrubs

Backyard composters; native perennial wildflower kits; worm castings; free self-serve wood chips; LEAF-subsidized Backyard Tree Planting Program; Backyard Habitat Certification; Richmond Hill Blooms garden recognition; community garden allotment plots
Eligible rainwater-recovery equipment: barrel or cistern, minimum 150 litres, above-ground or underground; gutter-connected
Cool roofs (new membrane or coating on existing roof) -- a roofing system with high solar reflectivity and thermal emissivity to reduce urban heat island effect.
Community gardens
Rain gardens
Cool roofs (reflective membrane or coating retrofits to reduce urban heat island); Green Roof Structural Assessment Grant (engineering assessment funding)

Eco-landscaping; rain barrel installation; window/door replacement; air sealing (incl. DIY air sealing kit); heat pump installation; backwater valve installation; basement flood alarm; climate resilience kit; DIY home energy savings kit (via Climate Ready Homes Program free home consultation incentives and Home Retrofit Pilot rebates)
Infiltration chambers; employee/public/student education

Infiltration galleries/soakaway pits/dry wells/French drains (residential); rooftop, parking lot and underground storage, stormwater management ponds (non-residential flood control); oil/grit separators, vegetated filter strips, salt management plan, paved area sweeping program (non-residential pollution control); education measures (up to 5% credit)

Vertical/wall gardens (vertikální zahrada); nature-close restoration of small watercourses, springs and wells (přírodě blízké úpravy drobných vodních toků, studánek a pramenů); infiltration terrain adjustments (úprava terénu pro podporu zasakování srážkové vody / zasakování na vhodném pozemku); revitalization of paved surfaces combined with green infrastructure (replacing impermeable surfaces); pupil-led research/citizen-science projects on rainwater and water in the landscape; creation of own teaching materials/programmes, excursions and teacher training on stormwater management

Facade planting beds (plantebede) with climbing plants and ground cover plants; optional pre-assembled 'solpakke' (sun package: climbing hydrangea, bloody cranesbill, wild garlic/wild strawberry) or 'skyggepakke' (shade package: ivy, common polypody, wild garlic/wild strawberry); competition/premiering for best-kept bed

Infiltration/detention measures: faskiner (soakaway pits/infiltration trenches), regnbede (rain gardens), gennemtrængelige belægninger (permeable paving), åbne bassiner (open wet/dry detention basins) as delay elements -- eligible for permit and, if disconnection is full, the connection-fee refund; plus downspout/surface disconnection from the public sewer (afkobling af regnvand fra kloak) and rainwater reuse for toilet flushing/laundry (genbrug af regnvand til toiletskyl og tøjvask, 0 kr. discharge fee)

Infiltration facilities such as soakaway/infiltration pit (faskine) or rain garden (regnbed); full disconnection of roof and surface water (tag- og overfladevand -- from house, carport, garage, sheds, driveway, terrace) from the combined sewer, carried out by an authorized licensed plumber (autoriseret kloakmester); requires a "Tilladelse til håndtering af regnvand på egen grund" permit; optional emergency overflow (nødoverløb) connection to BlueKolding's main sewer system permitted for extreme rain events (case-by-case approval, reduces refund to 75%)
Soakaways/infiltration installations

Faskiner (soakaway/infiltration trenches/crates) for roof and paved-surface runoff, with technical guidance on infiltration testing (K-value), sizing, and distance requirements; infiltration of roof water in the lawn (nedsivning af regnvand i græsplænen) for shed/greenhouse runoff; downspout/drain redirection to regnbed or faskine

Downspout disconnection (déconnexion de gouttière) from the public stormwater network, with overflow/trop-plein directed to a vegetated garden area for infiltration -- mandatory precondition for the rainwater harvester purchase subsidy

Infiltration under parking areas ("infiltrer vos eaux sous une place de parking"); permeable structures/infiltration basins ("structures perméables ou des bassins" favorisant l'infiltration); downspout/network disconnection (Brest métropole "déconnecte les réseaux d'eau"); rain garden, green roof, permeable parcel design ("jardin de pluie", "végétaliser une toiture", "rendre votre parcelle plus perméable")

Tree-pit greening scheme (végétalisation d'un pied d'arbre): planting limited to small perennials (vivaces) max 60cm height; climbing plants and any furniture/stake installations (tuteurs) excluded; requires signed occupation-of-public-domain agreement (convention) with the city, valid 1 year renewable
Rainwater harvesting/collection tank subsidies

Street-level "greening" via the "Rue Jardin" vegetalisation permit (resident-installed planters/pots, flowers, shrubs, climbing plants, vegetated tree pits on public street frontage, 3-year renewable AOT, using Mediterranean/low-water species and organic gardening methods, mineral fertilisers/phytosanitary products banned); plus collective/shared gardens ("jardins collectifs": jardins familiaux + jardins partagés, 90 sites on municipal land); plus tolerance/light management of urban wastelands as informal nature spaces (Friches Urbaines Naturelles, 300+ sites)

Jardins partagés (espaces collectifs jardinés par des associations de voisins, terrain mis à disposition gratuitement par la ville/OPHM via convention) ; micro-espaces de rue et pieds d'arbres adoptables (ex-"On sème à Montreuil") ; jardins familiaux (parcelles individuelles payantes, réduites à 75-90 m² depuis 2012, conventions de 5 ans) ; jardins d'insertion et jardins pédagogiques ; kits de jardinage (graines, outils) et matériaux (broyat, cuve à eau) fournis au lancement des projets ; formations au jardinage (semis, boutures, récolte de graines) ; Charte du Jardinier Urbain Responsable ; service de mise en relation jardiniers/parcelles disponibles ; trocs et dons de plantes/graines (trocs de plantes, groupe Facebook Montreuil Troc Végétal)
Downspout/gutter disconnection ('déraccordement de gouttière') incentivised via the higher rain-barrel subsidy rate.

Depaving/participatory planting of sidewalk plots ("Ma rue est un jardin": cutting pavement, planting perennials/climbers/ferns/succulents like ivy, jasmine, periwinkle) plus free native wildflower seed-sowing in pavement cracks and facades ("Ma rue en fleurs"), using local, low-water, pollinator-friendly meadow species

Stormwater desealing/desimperméabilisation works: disconnection of stormwater from the combined (unitary) sewer network to enable on-site infiltration, subsidised at €30/m² desealed (up to 50% of costs) -- de-sealing/infiltration-favouring land works
Rainwater harvesting barrel subsidy (50€ aid for rain barrels/récupérateurs d'eau de pluie)

Végétalisation en pied de façade (fosses réalisées par la collectivité et livrées avec terre végétale) ; végétalisation de petits espaces verts publics par un collectif associatif avec préparation du sol (décompactage, labourage) et irrigation si point d'eau existant
Street-facing wall-foot planting with climbing plants; planting-pit excavation and topsoil placement

Micro-implantations florales sur trottoir: citizen-led street-side flower micro-plantings, whereby the City breaks open the asphalt of a sidewalk to create a permeable planting bed; residents form a group of "jardiniers de rue," sign a végétalisation charter, and receive a Temporary Occupation Authorization (AOT) of public space to plant and maintain the bed using ecological, non-polluting gardening methods (all technical studies and works funded by the City).

Downspout collector kit ("kit collecteur de gouttière complet") included with each rain barrel, enabling roof-downspout connection; no other listed practices (infiltration pits, native planting, courtyard greening) are mentioned in the sources
Solardach-Kombination -- bonus for combining green roof (Gründach) with photovoltaic/solar-thermal installation ("Sonderform Solardach")

Rainwater cisterns (Regenwasserzisternen), infiltration/soakaway area design (Regenwasserversickerung), and depaving/desealing of concrete and asphalt surfaces (Entsiegelung). No other practice types (green roofs, façade greening, tree planting, rain gardens, bioswales) are named.

Retention/drainage elements on green roofs (Maßnahmen zur Erhöhung der Abflussverzögerung: Speicher-, Retentions- und Steuerungselemente); irrigation systems for facade greening (Bewässerungssysteme); raised beds (Hochbeete, min. 200L/0.5m height) where ground-bound planting is not technically possible; combination with solar PV (Gründach-PV)

Depaving/desealing of home garden and courtyard surfaces (Entsiegelung von Hausgarten- und Hofflächen, added 2023); greening of sloped/pitched roofs (Begrünung von Schrägdächern, added 2023) in addition to flat roofs; public info events and mobile demonstration unit ("Mobiles Grünes Zimmer") on building-based climate adaptation measures (dach- und Fassadenbegrünung, Hof-Entsiegelung)

Green roof construction requirement for water storage (min. 10cm substrate or ≥25L/m² storage capacity), funded in both combined (Mischsystem) and separate (Trennsystem) sewer catchment areas, including roofs of carports, extensions and garages; no other infiltration/downspout-disconnection/native-planting practices are supported

Facade greening (Fassadenbegrünung, ground- or wall-bound); depaving/desealing of surfaces (Entsiegelung von Flächen) with resulting stormwater to infiltrate on-site; rainwater and greywater reuse systems (Regenwasser- und Grauwassernutzungsanlagen) for toilet flushing/garden irrigation; infiltration of roof/overflow runoff required where soil conditions allow; free advisory consultation via Bremer Umwelt Beratung e.V.

Gärtnerische Gestaltung und Begrünung von Innenhöfen, Stellplätzen und Vorgärten sowie Dachbegrünung und Fassadenbegrünung (courtyard, parking-area and front-garden greening/planting design, plus green roofs and green façades); site-appropriate, sustainable (biodiversity-friendly) planting; free advisory consultation for owners on greening options and application support
No

Photovoltaik-Anlagen (PV solar installations) are also funded under the same 'Klimafreundliches Dormagen' programme alongside green roofs/façades; not itself an NbS measure but part of the same funding envelope.

Roof greening (extensive, min. 8cm substrate, native/perennial plants); ground- and wall-bound façade greening (wall-bound requires rainwater irrigation, native plants); and depaving of sealed surfaces with conversion to on-site infiltrating vegetation area, incl. disposal of old paving surface (must not be connected to sewer system)

Entsiegelung (depaving of paved/gravel garden areas) combined with naturnahe/native, site-appropriate, insect-friendly planting, funded under the "Mehr Grün für Duisburg" programme (alongside separate tree-planting and green-roof, incl. DIY green-roof kit, funding)
Innenhofbegrünung incl. play/path/seating areas and equipment; urban gardening projects on private land; removal of sealed surfaces; climbing aids, pergolas

Barrier-free/accessibility retrofits (widened entrances, ramps, tactile paving, handrails); shopfront/Ladenfront redesign (incl. canopies, floor-plan changes for retail attractiveness); structural/load-bearing measures to secure townscape-defining building fabric; residential surroundings design (Wohnumfeldgestaltung); façade greening (Fassade Begrünung) and roof greening (Dachbegrünung); partial architect/planning cost coverage (DIN 276 cost estimate, site supervision, completion certification)
No additional measures stated beyond extensive roof and façade greening in the current StädteRegion Aachen programme.

Depaving/desealing of private surfaces (paving stones, asphalt, concrete slabs -- garden, courtyard or driveway), min. 5 m², followed by planting incl. native species (e.g. Kornelkirsche, Felsenbirne, Feldahorn, Wildapfel); registered via abpflastern.de and/or by email to the city (klimaanpassung@flensburg.de), rewarded with a free tree/shrub from the city
Courtyard greening; technical shading in public/semi-public space; public drinking fountains; solar-green roofs
Rainwater retention/infiltration; cisterns; swales and swale-trench systems; native tree planting; biodiversity seed mixes; intensive/retention/biodiversity/solar green roofs

Insektenfreundliche Blühflächen (insect-friendly flowering areas ≥20m² cost-shared; <20m² seed supplied free by city); Baumpflegerische Maßnahmen (tree care/crown maintenance for trees ≥175cm circumference)

Vorgärten-/Innenhofbegrünung (front garden/courtyard greening); Pergolen, Rankhilfen, begrünte Eingangsbereiche/Torbögen (pergolas, climbing aids, greened entrances); bodengebundene Begrünung von Mauern, Zäunen, Müllplatzeinhausungen (ground-bound greening of walls, fences, bin enclosures); Einbau von Oberboden/Pflanzsubstraten für dauerhafte Begrünung; Ansaat extensiver Rasenmischungen, Blühwiesenflächen und Stauden (extensive lawn/wildflower/perennial seeding); Herstellung "grüner" Stellplätze mit Rasenwaben (green parking areas with grass-paver systems)
Rigolen; planted infiltration swales/depressions; flood-resilient property protection; external shading; water-fed cooling ceilings
Yes -- Courtyard greening (Hofbegrünung) explicitly funded alongside façade and roof greening

Green facade support (ground- and wall-bound systems, soil preparation/replacement, climbing aids/pergolas, planting, irrigation systems, own-labour by qualified professionals credited up to 60% of material costs) and solar-green roof combinations (Solar-Gründach): subsidy of €50/m² for reinforcing/adapting roof substructure to combine solar panels with green roofs, plus supplementary grants for improving load-bearing capacity of existing roofs for solar-green roofs
Unterkonstruktion für Solar-Gründach und Förderung zur Verbesserung der Tragfähigkeit von Bestandsdächern für Solar-Gründach

Greening of walls, bin enclosures (Mülltonneneinhausungen) and carports; conversion of gravel gardens (Schottergärten) into near-natural front gardens (naturnahe Vorgärten); near-natural/naturalistic garden design more generally (naturnahe Gartengestaltung)
Structural check/calculation subsidy (up to €450); prior professional advisory consultation on greening, up to €200, or up to €400 if combined with PV
Courtyard greening; full and partial depaving; solar green roofs; biodiversity green roofs; retention green roofs; freestanding vertical greening; publicly accessible drinking-water fountains

Green roof vegetation build-up (protective layer, filter fleece, shear protection above 10° slope, drainage layer, substrate layer 6-15cm, planting/seeding with site-appropriate, insect-friendly species); removal of ground cover and soil preparation for ground-bound façade greening systems, climbing aids/façade greening systems, and planting measures; excludes roof waterproofing and mere installation of plant pots/planters; planning and installation must be by verifiably qualified external professionals
das Anlegen von insektenfreundlichen Grünflächen

Freiflächenentsiegelung (de-sealing of paved courtyards/open areas), required as precondition for follow-on greening; removal/greening of Schottergärten (gravel gardens); perennial beds (Staudenbeete); meadow/lawn areas (Wiesen- und Rasenflächen); tree and shrub planting (Baum- und Strauchbepflanzungen); plus bundled advisory service (Beratung) from pre-application through completion of the measure
Raised beds and permanent planters; pergolas; improved roof access associated with the funded greening

Other supported practices in Kiel's green roof/facade program include: (1) irrigation systems (Bewässerungssysteme) for facade greening; (2) root-penetration protection film/root-resistant membrane (Durchwurzelschutz / Folie mit Wurzelfestigkeit) as an add-on surcharge for green roofs, distinct from standard sealing; (3) structural load-bearing (Statik/Tragfähigkeit) upgrades for green roofs on existing buildings; (4) a "Solar-Gründach" surcharge for the extra cost of mounting solar PV systems on a combined green roof; and (5) the "Kieler Naturdach" regional/native seed mix recommended for extensive green roofs.

Other supported practices under GRÜN hoch³ include: (1) Entsiegelung and Rückbau von Schotterflächen (deconstruction of gravel/rock gardens with subsequent unsealing and greening) as a distinct funded measure; (2) combination of green roof with cistern (with overflow) and/or Rigole (infiltration trench/soakaway) to decouple areas from the sewer network and qualify for stormwater fee adjustment; (3) Fertigstellungspflege (establishment/completion maintenance) co-funded as part of the commissioned green-roof measure; (4) Biodiversitätsgründach / biodiversity bonus elements -- native insect-friendly planting, deadwood piles, sand lenses -- funded via flat-rate bonus (150€/300€) in addition to base extensive greening; (5) Solar-Gründach (combined green roof + PV) supported as a technical design variant; (6) Retentionsgründach (retention green roof with plastic water-retention boxes) technically supported/recognized as part of the rootable layer thickness.

PV systems (rooftop/new-build and plug-in balcony PV), battery storage, private EV wallboxes, and individually-assessed "klimafreundliche Sondermaßnahmen" (climate-friendly special measures) -- which explicitly include facade greening (Fassadenbegrünung) and smart-metering/grid adaptation for tenant-electricity (Mieterstrom) models in multi-family PV buildings; social funding tier subsidises balcony-PV for low-income households. Green roofs (Dachbegrünung) are funded as a separate standard category alongside these.
Nature-oriented garden redesign; ecologically valuable trees, shrubs, perennials and wildflowers

Structural (Statik) check/calculation funding (up to €450); prior professional greening advisory consultation funding (up to €200); combined PV-with-green-roof incentive (higher subsidy, up to €400 additional for PV cases)
De-sealing (Entsiegelung) of paved/impermeable surfaces and building greening (Gebäudebegrünung), funded under the wider "grün-blaue Infrastruktur" (green-blue infrastructure) directive

Dry-stone wall (Trockenmauer/Weinbergstaffel) restoration & new construction in vineyard terraces (§2.3, 100 EUR/m² or per linear metre, cap 10,000 EUR/year/applicant); Naturschutzprojekte und Artenhilfsmaßnahmen incl. creation/maintenance of ecologically valuable biotope areas, dry-stone wall restoration in outdoor areas, and procurement/installation of nesting aids (§2.9, 100% of agreed plant material + 50% other material/installation costs, cap 500 EUR/measure/year); geothermal heat probe drilling/Erdwärmesonden borehole funding (§2.11, 6 EUR/borehole metre, cap 1,000 EUR/project)
Flowering areas and seed mixtures; woody planting within supported front-garden greening

Green roofs (via Lippeverband's "10.000 Grüne Dächer" regional funding programme referral); tree sponsorship (Baumpatenschaft); informational guidance on gravel-free/colourful front gardens (Bunte Vorgärten)

Free/neutral consultation on greening and depaving measures (feasibility, structural/Statik, funding); climate-adapted/native planting advice; courtyard and front-garden greening (blühende Hinterhöfe und Vorgärten, Vorgarten-Entsiegelung); vertical gardens and green roof terraces promoted; green roof cadastre (Gründachkataster) linked with solar roof cadastre for synergy analysis
Preparatory depaving and soil preparation for façade greening; climbing aids, façade systems and pergolas
Courtyard depaving/garden landscaping; façade greening; rainwater use (barrels/cisterns/ponds); tenant gardens

Entsiegelung von Flächen (depaving/desealing); ökologische, ortsbildgerechte Gartengestaltung mit heimischen Pflanzen und Beeten (native/ecological planting); Reaktivierung des Bodens und Bereitstellung von Gartenland für Mieter- und Gemeinschaftsgärten (soil reactivation/community & tenant gardens); barrierefreie Zugangsgestaltung (accessible access); Begrünung von Mauern (wall greening); historisch materialgerechte Erhaltung/Erneuerung von Mauern, Toren, Einfriedungen (heritage-appropriate wall/gate/enclosure preservation); Entrümplung und Abbruch nicht erhaltenswerter baulicher Außenanlagen (clearance/demolition of non-heritage outbuildings)

Naturnahe Begrünung von Firmengeländen (nature-near greening of company/commercial premises with native trees, shrubs, grasses); courtyard greening (Innenhofbegrünung); front-garden greening (Vorgartenbegrünung); desealing/depaving combined with greening or permeable surfacing

Entsiegelung der Hofflächen; Herstellung von Grünflächen, Wegen und Plätzen; Bepflanzungsmaßnahmen; Begrünung von Mauern, Wand- und Dachflächen; Abbruch brachgefallener Bausubstanz im Innenhof (Fassadensanierung selbst codiert unter separatem Fassaden-Item, nicht E-7)

Flächenentsiegelung; Zisterne; Gründach / Fassadenbegrünung; Gartenumgestaltung (gravel-dominated gardens converted into biologisch höherwertige Lebensräume); €300 bonus for Anschluss der Zisterne an Haushaltsgeräte/WC

Planning/design costs; biodiversity measures and nesting/breeding habitats (Brut- und Nisthilfen); green pergolas/trellises (Begrünte Pergolen/Rankgerüste); greening of new garage/carport builds and subordinate extensions; natural children's play areas as part of desealing (sand, fine gravel, wood/bark surfacing)

Entsiegelung und Begrünung versiegelter Flächen (Parkplätze, Innenhöfe, (Vor-)Gärten), inkl. Teilentsiegelung mit versickerungsfähigen Belägen (Schotterrasen, Fahrspuren, Rasengitter-/Rasenkammersteine, Rasenfugenpflaster, großfugiges Natursteinpflaster, Kies-/Splittdecken; max. 50% der Fläche, s. Anlage 2); intensive/begehbare Dachgärten mit Retentionsauflage (Abflussbeiwert ≥0,3, ≥35% Nettovegetationsfläche, Zugänglichkeitsauflage); statische Ertüchtigung des Daches im Zusammenhang mit Dachbegrünung
Courtyard and parking-lot depaving/greening

Covers the rain-barrel unit only . Delivery is separately available for $24. Installation, design, permitting, maintenance and monitoring support are not stated.

Covers: purchase cost of rain barrel storage container only (up to $50 or purchase price if less), original sale only, max 3 per household. Excludes: accessories/add-ons (stands, diverters, downspout kits, hoses, filters, rain chains), resale/private-sale purchases, installation labour/maintenance costs

Covers: subsidised/at-cost purchase price of physical equipment only (rain barrel, water timer, backyard composter, kitchen catcher); pick-up logistics (by appointment at City Hall or Animal Shelter). Excludes: installation labour, plumbing/permitting costs (note a Plumbing Permit may be separately required for certain rain barrel uses per National Plumbing Code amendments), ongoing maintenance, and any monitoring costs -- none of these are covered or mentioned as covered by the City
Covers 50% of eligible new-product purchase costs up to CAD 150, or 75% up to CAD 200 for local purchases; minimum purchase CAD 50

Covers rebates (based on receipts) toward the cost of eligible RainWise stormwater management materials/equipment and contractor installation labour for downspout disconnection, rain barrels/storage tanks (and accessories), rain gardens/box planters, soakaway pits, permeable pavement, and (multi-family/ICI only) absorbent landscaping and soil cells, up to per-project rebate formulas and per-property annual caps varying by customer type ($2,000 single-family; $5,000 multi-family; $10,000 ICI). Excludes: stormwater installations required for property development/compliance; work completed before application approval (not retroactive); new eaves; purely decorative materials; and (not documented as covered) ongoing maintenance/monitoring and design/permitting costs beyond the required application design sketch.

Covers invoiced purchase or installation costs for listed RIISP measures, subject to percentage and dollar caps; labour, materials and taxes are explicitly included where stated. Property must be connected to the municipal sanitary sewer. Other cost categories are not stated.

Covers: for the seasonal system, an approved outdoor rainwater harvesting tank (≥500L, includes leaf screen, hose, small pump) via a one-time rebate of $0.50/litre of tank storage up to $2,000; for the all-season system, an approved indoor/outdoor cistern/tank-based system with treatment components, via a flat $2,000 rebate plus Blue Built Home certification. Excludes: rain barrels and repurposed/homemade tanks (explicitly ineligible for either program); ongoing maintenance costs; and, though not explicitly labeled "excluded," building permit fees and engineer/plumbing contractor design-and-install costs are not listed among reimbursed items and are described as the applicant's responsibility to obtain/hire .

Covers: reduction of the Site Related Flow Charge (stormwater utility fee) for Non-Residential properties operating qualifying peak-flow-detention BMPs on an ongoing basis. Excludes: no coverage of capital/installation costs, no maintenance cash grants, and Residential Property customers are not eligible for this credit (only Non-Residential per s.7(8)); Residential customers instead pay a flat tiered Site Related Flow Charge (Table 4A(ii)) with no credit mechanism stated.

Approved materials, design/professional services, installation labour, permits/locates, excavation and specified enabling works; excludes decorative items, tools, machinery, DIY labour, gutters/eavestroughs and non-permeable paving

Covers portions of landscape/irrigation design, climate-appropriate plants, growing medium, mulch/soil amendments, permeable landscape materials and irrigation equipment. Excludes previously unlandscaped areas, retroactive expenditure and uncompleted approved measures.

Covers: repurposed 220 L barrel, filter basket, tap, overflow adaptor/hose, HST, delivery and a two-year parts warranty, sold at Utilities Kingston's cost. Excludes: resident installation labour and programme-paid maintenance.

Covers: percentage reduction of the stormwater portion of the monthly utility bill for property owners who install/maintain approved BMPs (rain barrels, cisterns, infiltration galleries, rain gardens, permeable pavers for residential; plus quality/quantity/education measures for non-residential). Excludes: new development/redevelopment project fees, off-site or City-easement BMPs, design/permitting/monitoring costs, and any direct cash payment or capital cost reimbursement (no money changes hands -- only a bill-fee percentage reduction)

Covers, at 75% of pre-tax purchase cost: eligible plants/shrubs, plus a defined list of eligible materials (compost, manure, mycorrhizae, natural uncoloured mulch/wood chips, ramial chipped wood, geotextile/geomembrane, insect-hotel materials) and delivery fees -- with materials+delivery capped at 25% of plant costs (max $105 façade garden / $160 riverside garden), and an overall grant maximum of $400 (façade) or $600 (riverside). Excludes seeds, bulbs, trees, black/garden soil, sphagnum moss, coloured mulch/wood chips, tools, fertilizer, stakes, edging, stones/slabs, any other unlisted material, and all labour costs.

Covers: 50% of the pre-tax purchase price of a new low-flow toilet (≤6 LPF/1.6 GPF) or new rain barrel (incl. DIY rain-barrel assembly kit cost only, not barrel-building materials), up to $100 per item, max 2 toilets and 2 rain barrels per household ($400 max total), for items purchased new in Canada (or from a Canadian online distributor) during the program term. Excludes: installation, delivery/shipping fees, GST/taxes; excludes ICI (industrial/commercial/institutional) customers and condo/apartment buildings billed via condo fees.

Covers: subsidised purchase price of a 200 L recycled food-grade rain barrel (écobaril) for rainwater harvesting/gardening use, reducing potable water consumption. Excludes: installation/plumbing beyond barrel acquisition, downspout modification, maintenance, and any other NbS measure types (green roofs, façades, rain gardens, permeable paving, trees) not offered under this programme.

Covers: free distribution of trees; discounted (reduced-price) purchase of composters and rainwater barrels/récupérateurs; distribution of miscellaneous kits and compost; educational wastewater-plant tour and family activities. Excludes: no coverage of green roofs, façades, rain gardens, permeable paving, installation labour, design/permitting, or ongoing maintenance costs.

Covers: purchase cost (50% of price, up to item-specific caps) of eligible rainwater capture devices (rain barrels/downspout diverters up to $200/unit, max 2; rain cisterns $250/unit, max 1 -- cisterns require professional installation), xeriscaping/drought-tolerant landscaping materials (organic mulch, landscape rock, eco-friendly artificial turf, native trees/shrubs, native grass seed mixes, non-turf ground-cover, weed-barrier landscape fabric, each up to $100-$500), home composting units (up to $150/unit, max 1), drip irrigation components (up to $100), and smart (soil-moisture/weather-based) irrigation controllers (up to $150) -- all subject to an overall $1,000/household lifetime maximum. Excludes: traditional/synthetic artificial turf, concrete pavers and patio stones, materials for driveways/dog runs/under structures (e.g., decks), countertop composters/electronic composter systems and their accessories, and non-smart home irrigation system controllers/timers; condominium associations are also ineligible (treated as commercial).
No construction costs covered; reduction is based on verified peak flow, water-quality, runoff-volume and operational performance

Covers per-item grant amounts (set dollar amounts per unit of work, e.g. per linear metre/panel/door) for specified eligible work categories under Block 1 (foundations, green roof, plumbing, landscaping, garage entrance, heating/AC, electricity, watertight door, metal flood barrier), Block 2 (adds envelope, roofing, windows/doors/balconies, ventilation), and Block 3 flood-protection-only work; excludes non-listed work items, permit fees/permit procurement (owner's separate responsibility), and is not full reimbursement of total project cost -- grants are capped per-work-item up to an overall building cap ($26,000 single-family; $52,000 for 2-5 unit buildings, x1.5 for co-ops/non-profits); subsidy amounts received must be deducted from rent calculations for tenants

Covers: purchase and installation of a potable-use-rated cistern (≥4,546 L) and associated collection-system components (transport piping, debris traps, filters, installation labour), up to $1,000/household total. Excludes: distribution components beyond the tank (e.g., indoor plumbing distribution), rain barrels (too small to qualify), retroactive purchases from prior calendar years, and more than one rebate per property over the programme's lifetime.

Covers: subsidised purchase price of the 208L rain barrel unit itself ($76 + GST), which is a single-measure programme (rain barrel purchase only) -- the "Rain Barrel Program" does not fund/cover green infrastructure such as green roofs, façades, rain gardens, permeable paving, or trees. Excludes: installation labour, design/planning, permitting, monitoring, ongoing maintenance, and explicitly excludes replacement of barrels damaged due to improper (e.g., winter) storage.

Covers: partial cost of one native backyard tree (purchase price top-up of $100) via LEAF's Full Service Backyard Tree Planting program (site consultation, delivery, planting, mulch, care guide, follow-up advice). Excludes: front-yard/unfenced side-yard plantings (LEAF full-service only plants in backyards/fenced side yards), shrubs/cedars (only trees receive the extra $100), ongoing watering/maintenance costs, more than one subsidized tree per property, and any structural stormwater measures (rain gardens, permeable paving, cisterns) which are only supported for commercial/industrial properties under the separate Stormwater Credit Program.

Flat area-based incentive rather than a share of actual costs: green roof $100.00/m² installed up to $100,000 per project; cool roof with new membrane $5.00/m² up to $50,000; cool roof coating over existing roof $2.00/m² up to $50,000; plus a Structural Assessment Grant equal to the actual cost or $1,000, whichever is less. Applicant must submit documentation of the full cost of installation. Parking garages and at-grade roofs are ineligible; renewable-energy areas, private terraces and residential outdoor amenities (max 2 m²/unit) are excluded from available roof space. Permits and all construction, maintenance and repair remain the applicant's responsibility.

Covers (eligible costs, per measure): Downspout redirection -- materials for redirecting existing downspouts (extenders/hardware), erosion prevention materials at outlet (splash pad/rocks), disconnection/redirection materials from storm or combined sewers, materials/labour to alter ground-level surfacing to facilitate redirection, and rain barrels incorporated as part of redirection; Rain gardens -- rebate based on final installed garden area (not receipts); Soakaway pits -- rebate based on DCIA managed (not receipts); Permeable pavement -- rebate based on installed permeable surface area (not receipts); Certified Fusion Landscape Design -- design services provided by a certified Fusion Landscape Professional. Excludes: new eavestrough installation materials; purely/solely decorative materials; non-depressed (non-infiltrating) portions of rain gardens; non-permeable pavement areas; design services from a non-certified landscape professional and any services/materials unrelated to the Fusion Landscape design; and, structurally, any work/address outside a priority stormwater retrofit area (geographic eligibility is a threshold requirement, not a cost-coverage exclusion, but no costs are reimbursed outside it).

Covers: reimbursement (up to $1,000, based on stormwater capture/storage volume calculated from roof area) toward cost of eligible installation materials (plants, stone, topsoil) and/or cost of hiring a professional landscaper/contractor to install the rain garden. Excludes: tools (shovels, rakes, wheelbarrows) [stated]; design/planning, permitting, ongoing maintenance, and monitoring costs are not listed as reimbursable items
Covers subsidized native tree/shrub purchase and optional full-service planting; other cost categories not stated

Covers 50% of the purchase cost of a new rain barrel (up to $50/barrel, max 2 per utility account lifetime); excludes installation labour costs, hoses/accessories, maintenance, and any costs beyond the barrel purchase itself; requires proof of purchase receipt and City utility account

Covered items (list-based, per theme, "Voici les subventions offertes en lien avec..."): biodiversité/verdissement (potager, serre, plantation d'arbre, pelouse durable mixte); gestion de l'eau (baril récupérateur d'eau de pluie, toilette et équipements de plomberie à faible débit); gestion des matières résiduelles... Excluded/not covered: design, permitting, ongoing maintenance and monitoring costs are not listed as covered

Covers only the subsidised purchase price ($30 CAD) of a single 208-litre SYSTERN rain barrel (with mosquito mesh, UV stabilizer, overflow hose) sold at the City Recycling Depot, plus included installation instructions; excludes design/planning, permitting, ongoing maintenance and monitoring costs, and excludes all other stormwater NbS measures (green roofs, green façades, rain gardens, permeable paving, tree planting)

Covers: subsidised purchase price of native trees/shrubs, wildflower kits, rain barrels, composters, worm castings; subsidised professional planting service (arborist consultation, tree, mulch, delivery, planting labour via LEAF); free self-serve wood chips. Excludes: ongoing watering/maintenance after delivery, plant replacement/refunds ('no refunds or exchanges', city 'not responsible for plant material that does not survive')
Covers purchase price of an approved rain barrel/cistern of at least 150 litres; transport and delivery excluded
Covers/provides the 220-litre barrel at a fixed $22 purchase price ; installation, plumbing and maintenance coverage not stated
Covers ready-made rain-barrel purchase or DIY construction supplies; receipts required

Covers: installation cost of green/cool roof (per m²), structural assessment for green roofs (up to $1,000). Excludes: ongoing maintenance costs, design/permitting fees (though permit is required, not separately funded), and costs beyond project caps ($100,000 green roof; $50,000 cool roof).
Covers purchase of one rain barrel per household per year
Covers the rain-barrel unit at CAD 70 including GST, maximum two per person; other costs Not stated

Covers up to half of eligible community-garden start-up costs, including lumber, soil, seeds, rain barrels, other materials and necessary tools; applicants are incorporated charities, not-for-profits, unincorporated associations or neighbourhood groups
Covers 80% of the pre-tax purchase cost of a new domestic rainwater harvester, capped at $100 CAD per eligible property; accessories, installation/use products and gutter modifications are excluded
Covers eligible plants, soil amendments, gravel/rock, edging and other pre-approved landscaping expenses; reimbursement up to $625

Covers: installation costs of the eco-roof itself -- green roof vegetated area at $100/m² (max $100,000) and cool roof surface at $5/m² new membrane or $2/m² coating (max $50,000) -- plus, for green roofs only, a Structural Assessment Grant equal to the cost of the assessment up to $1,000. Excludes: maintenance costs, planter boxes (not considered an extension of the roofing system), at-grade/parking-garage roofs, permit/permitting costs, and any work started or completed before funding approval.

Covers: (1) free 60-90 min home consultations plus one free in-kind incentive item per household (rain barrel, tree/shrub, DIY energy/air-sealing kit, basement flood alarm, or climate resilience kit) -- available to single-family detached/semi-detached/townhome residents within the Thornhill SNAP boundaries (addresses verified); and (2) separately, a now-closed 10-household Home Retrofit Pilot that covered free retrofit coaching plus up to $3,800 in rebates toward retrofit actions (window/door replacement, air sealing, heat pump installation, backwater valve installation, rain barrel installation, eco-landscaping). Excludes: costs beyond the $3,800 rebate cap, and any coverage of design/permitting fees, ongoing maintenance, or monitoring costs (not mentioned); program restricted to eligible single-family home types within Thornhill SNAP boundaries; retrofit pilot capped at 10 households and applications now closed.

Covers: (1) one-time rebates ($35-$1,500) toward upfront/installation costs of approved rainwater management methods (rain barrels, cisterns, rain gardens, infiltration chambers, permeable paving; bioswales via professional) -- available only to owner-occupied low-density residential (1-4 unit) properties; and (2) ongoing annual stormwater utility bill credits -- a flat 10% for all low-density residential properties, and tiered 2.5-50% credits for multi-family/business/institutional properties based on method and % of roof/impervious area treated (cisterns, green roofs, permeable paving, infiltration/rain gardens/bioswales, plus education credits for business/institutional). Excludes: rebates for multi-family/business/institutional and non-owner-occupied low-density properties (credit only, no rebate); design/planning, permitting, and monitoring costs (not mentioned as covered); ongoing maintenance costs (not mentioned as covered). Professional installation is required for bioswales and for all multi-family/business/institutional projects.

Covers: reduction of the recurring stormwater utility charge based on installed stormwater management practices (rain barrels/cisterns, infiltration galleries, permeable pavers, rain gardens for residential; rooftop/parking lot/underground storage, ponds, green roofs, bioswales, oil/grit separators, salt management, sweeping programs, education measures for multi-unit/non-residential). Excludes: capital cost of purchasing/installing the practices themselves, ongoing maintenance costs, and any design/permitting fees -- these remain the property owner's responsibility.
Covers purchase of one eligible rain barrel up to $120; applicant is responsible for installation and maintenance

Covers: all costs directly and exclusively linked to supply/installation of the green roof vegetation build-up (waterproofing protection, root barriers, separation geotextiles, water-management layers, drainage layer, filter textile, retention/accumulation layer, substrate, vegetation, edge/gravel strips, additional drainage strips, shaft/cistern for green roofs, gravel for backfill, transport of substrate/plants/gravel/material, rental of handling equipment, laying works, adjustments to internal utility-water plumbing, connection to electricity supply), plus expert report costs up to 10,000 Kč for Group A applicants (replaced by building-permit design documentation for new builds, which is itself not eligible). VAT is eligible only where the applicant cannot reclaim input VAT (non-VAT-payers or no deduction right); otherwise it must be excluded and any VAT wrongly included must be refunded. Excludes: photovoltaic panels and associated material (even for biosolar roofs) as a hard exclusion regardless of applicant group; self-build (DIY) labour costs, except material purchase and necessary tool-rental costs; and post-installation costs are not addressed as a coverage item (5-year sustainability is a compliance/monitoring obligation, not a cost-coverage exclusion) -- treat maintenance/monitoring cost exclusion as Not stated rather than an affirmatively excluded cost category.

Covers: green roof design/structural assessment and installation, rain gardens/infiltration terrain works, rainwater storage vessels/ponds, permeable surface conversion, vertical gardens, natural watercourse restoration, educational materials/equipment (thermometers, rain gauges), staff wages, excursions, and educator training on stormwater topics. Excludes: equipment not installed/used on the school/organization's premises, one-off events, catering/refreshments, prizes/gifts for competitions, foreign travel expenses, leasing, rentals, and purchase/repair of computing or other electronic/communication devices (PCs, cameras, phones, copiers, laminators, etc.)

Covered (in-kind, no cash grant): municipal excavation/construction of the facade planting bed itself (three fixed sizes, 0.5m deep), carried out by the City's own operations organisation, plus optional free plant packages (sun or shade package, matched to bed size) if the applicant does not want to source/pay for plants themselves. Excluded: cash payments; plants if the applicant chooses their own; and all ongoing responsibilities -- planting labour, watering, pruning/tying-up, weeding, and facade-crack monitoring -- which are explicitly the applicant's responsibility under the mandatory cooperation agreement ("Du planter og plejer"). Scope is also structurally limited to beds the municipality itself establishes, targeted at streets not already characterised by greenery.

Covers: refund of the one-off sewer connection fee (tilslutningsbidrag) for stormwater disconnected to on-site infiltration (faskine, regnbed, permeable paving, basins), and waiver of the ongoing wastewater discharge fee (vandafledningsafgift) for reused rainwater (toilet/laundry), plus low fixed annual meter rental (80 kr excl. moms) for the reuse meter. Excludes: cost of designing, purchasing, or installing the infiltration/reuse system itself (borne by applicant/property owner), cost of required autoriseret kloakmester work, and any soil/groundwater contamination investigation costs on contaminated sites (explicitly stated to be borne by the applicant).

Covers: partial/full refund of the one-time sewer connection fee (tilslutningsbidrag) for rainwater, scaled to how much roof/surface water is disconnected from the main sewer (100% = full refund, emergency overflow = 75%, rear-only disconnection in row houses = 50%). Excludes: cost of building the on-site rainwater system itself (regnbed, faskine, plumber's disconnection work), ongoing maintenance, and there is no separate installation grant -- only reimbursement of the previously paid municipal/utility connection fee.
Covers a refund of the sewer connection contribution (up to 40% for full disconnection; pro-rata partial refund) plus regulatory/technical support

Covers technical/administrative support and, where Chapter 5 conditions are met, refund up to 40% of the sewer connection contribution for roof/surface-water disconnection; construction/disconnection work remains owner-paid unless otherwise stated
Purchase of a new CE-compliant rainwater harvester plus base, tap and connection kit; pressure-boosting equipment excluded

Covers the tax-included purchase cost of an eligible >=200L rainwater collector or >=2,000L buried cistern at 50%, subject to the stated EUR 150/EUR 500 caps and one aid per fiscal household; no other cost types are stated

Covered: purchase price of a new (min. 200L) rainwater harvester plus required accessories purchased at time of acquisition (connection/overflow kit, downspout collection device, filtration system) -- reimbursed at up to 80% of purchase price, capped by tank-size tier (€260/€310/€360). Eligible only if at least one gutter is permanently disconnected from the public stormwater network and the overflow is redirected to a garden/green space. Excluded/conditions: units purchased before 2 May 2024; second-hand/used tanks; tanks where the gutter was not previously connected to the public stormwater network; more than 2 units per dwelling (max. one per disconnected gutter, 2 gutters max per dwelling); combination with another organisation's subsidy (no cumulation). Labour/installation costs are not listed as a reimbursed cost item ; maintenance costs are not covered .

Covers acquisition and installation (achat et pose) of buried or integrated rainwater harvesting systems, conditional on the property owner/co-ownership syndic having already received the Département's Green Deal rainwater-harvester aid; excludes above-ground/non-integrated rain barrels and all other NbS measures (no mention of green roofs, façades, permeable paving, trees, or rain gardens).

Covers: 50% of the purchase price of one or more rainwater storage cisterns (outdoor use only, e.g. garden watering), bought in a single purchase, capped at €100 per household, non-renewable. Excludes: installation labour, plumbing/connection work, maintenance, permitting, and monitoring costs are not mentioned as covered.

Covers: for selected applicants (property owners in the 8 communes, chosen via the appel à projets) -- project design, technical analysis, and financial aid ("aide financière") for garden-based rainwater management measures (rain gardens, green roofs, permeable surfacing, parking-lot infiltration); separately, for all residents -- rain barrels/cisterns ("récupérateurs d'eaux pluviales") at preferential purchase prices (subsidised price, not free). Excludes/Not stated: no cost caps, no cost-category breakdown (design vs. installation vs. materials), and no mention of coverage for ongoing maintenance, monitoring, or permitting/connection fees.

Covers: authorization/permit to occupy public domain (pied d'arbre) for planting small perennials, city feasibility review, and issuance of a renewable 1-year occupation agreement. Excludes: any purchase of plants/materials, installation labour, financial support, and maintenance costs -- all borne by the applicant, who is also liable for damages from the installation.

Covers 80% of the purchase price ("prix d'achat"/"dépense globale") of a rainwater harvesting cistern and its accessories, capped by dwelling type: individual house (≥300L cistern) capped at €150; copropriété ≤10 units (≥1500L) capped at €650; copropriété >10 units (≥3000L) capped at €1500. Excludes: purchases before 1 Dec 2023 (not retroactive); any costs beyond cistern+accessories (no installation labour, design, permitting, or maintenance costs mentioned); and, by silence, all other NbS/water-saving measures (green roofs, façades, permeable paving, etc.) which are not covered by this scheme.
Covers 30% of the paid purchase cost of a new rainwater collector and ancillary connection equipment, tap, base and lid, subject to the EUR 100 minimum and EUR 500 maximum aid
Purchase cost of rainwater-recovery equipment and accessories only

Covers: purchase price (TTC) of the rainwater harvester tank(s) plus ancillary connection equipment (fittings, tap, base, cover), up to 80% of cost and capped at €50 per household, only for in-store (not online) purchases from a professional retailer before 31 Dec 2026. Excludes: installation labour costs (borne by the user), online purchases, and purchases by professionals/companies/associations other than family-garden associations.

Covers: initial free plant/vegetal distribution, provision of soil, city-executed technical works/studies for the plantation, and technical guidance/site visits for street-garden (jardin de rue), tree-pit, façade, and courtyard greening projects. Excludes: ongoing maintenance costs (citizen/association bears upkeep for the 5-year management term); no cash grants, tax rebates or loans documented.

Covers: free supply of initial plant stock (in a limited proposed range) at first installation, the permit/authorisation to occupy public space for 3 years (renewable), and provision of guides/technical advice for planning and species choice. Excludes: cash grants, tax rebates, loans, maintenance funding, and monitoring/permitting costs beyond the initial permit review -- resident bears installation labor, containers, ongoing watering/maintenance, and any costs beyond the initial free plant range.

Covers: purchase of a rainwater harvesting cistern/butt of minimum 300L capacity, via a €50 voucher redeemable at listed partner retailers (Brico Dépôt, Castorama, Magasin Vert, PUM Plastique). Excludes: installation labour costs, plumbing/gutter connection work, and any construction-related infiltration works (which fall under the separate Plan Pluie regulatory requirement for urbanism projects, not this voucher scheme). Requires proof of residence, syndic attestation (collective housing) or landlord authorisation (tenants), and photo of installation site.

Covers: purchase price (TTC/incl. tax) of a rainwater harvester, subsidised at up to €50 (or the actual purchase price if lower than €50); income-conditional (revenu fiscal de référence par part ≤€14,089 per the 2024-2026 règlement; the website currently states ≤€15,400, an apparent later update/discrepancy); limited to one grant per household (same address) over the 2024-2026 period. Excludes: installation/connection/plumbing labour, delivery, maintenance and monitoring costs, and any second application per household within the period (none of these are listed as reimbursable in the règlement or webpage).
Covers 50% of the paid purchase price of one eligible above-ground rainwater collector per household, capped at EUR 50 including tax

Covers (in-kind support only, no monetary grants): free provision of public/social-landlord land via temporary occupation convention (convention d'occupation temporaire) for shared gardens, family gardens and adopted street micro-spaces; administrative/technical support (project validation, advice, convention signing) by the Service Jardins et Nature en Ville; training sessions (sowing, cuttings, seed harvesting); materials (wood-chip mulch, water cisterns for shared gardens); appropriate signage; free starter gardening kits (seeds, hand tools) at project launch; planting of fruit trees in public space by municipal gardeners; and continued maintenance by municipal gardeners only on spaces not taken up by residents. Excludes: direct cash grants/subsidies, tax or bill rebates, loans, subsidized purchase of individual/ongoing equipment beyond the launch kit, and ongoing maintenance funding for resident-run plots (upkeep is the residents' responsibility under the signed charter/convention).
Covered: purchase of eligible above-ground tank(s) plus accessories in one physical-store transaction; online/underground purchases excluded.

Covers: sidewalk cutting/depaving labour, plant material and free wildflower seed packets, initial technical guidance/site visit from city gardeners. Excludes: ongoing watering/maintenance labour or supplies after installation, which residents must provide themselves under the signed charter.

Covers: de-connection/desimperméabilisation works (dé-raccordement des eaux pluviales du réseau unitaire) on properties within Rennes Métropole member communes with combined sewer network, up to 50% of costs at €30/m² desimperméabilisé within applicable caps. Excludes/not addressed: new-construction stormwater management obligations (rainwater recovery structures, infiltration/retention works for >40m² footprint projects), which are separate regulatory requirements not funded by this aid.

Covers 50% of acquisition cost for an eligible rainwater collector/cistern and its listed connection, collection, filtration, tap or pumping accessories, subject to the applicable EUR 150 or EUR 1,000 cap
Covered: acquisition of new rainwater harvester (≥300 L capacity), up to €50 max. Excluded: installation, maintenance, and monitoring costs

Covers: pre-project studies/design, desealing/depaving works, tree/shrub/perennial purchase & planting, green roof installation (extensive/intensive/semi-intensive/bio-solar), green façade planting, rainwater cistern and wildlife shelter installation, and awareness/training 'animation' actions -- all as % of eligible cost with per-measure and per-project (€20,000) caps. Excludes: already-financed projects, projects fulfilling regulatory obligations, recently-built constructions, irrigation installation, plant maintenance/upkeep, invasive exotic species or monospecific hedges, and off-ground (hors sol) plantings.

Covers: construction of façade/tree planting pits (fosses) on public space, delivery of topsoil, plant guides/advice, one free climbing plant per pit (seasonal distribution, subject to stock); soil decompaction/ploughing and irrigation setup for collective public-space greening. Excludes: purchase cost of most plants/flowers (citizen buys or self-sources), ongoing watering/maintenance labour, and any cash reimbursement.
One climbing plant, joint planting, topsoil, necessary pavement excavation and administrative/technical coordination; resident covers wall supports and maintenance

Covers: technical/engineering study and physical works to break open sidewalk asphalt and prepare permeable in-ground planting space (installation only), plus the administrative permitting process (AOT). Excludes: cost of plants, gardening tools/supplies, and ongoing maintenance/watering, which are the residents' responsibility.

Covers one free 350 L harvester plus gutter-collector kit for eligible detached houses, qualifying ground-floor apartments, and family/shared gardens; 7,000 units in 2026, one kit per household/parcel while stocks last

Covers eligible roof/façade greening on both new and existing buildings where voluntary/not legally mandated; includes specified planning/material/construction and first-year completion-care costs; programme currently suspended until further notice

Covers green roof installation (Dachbegrünung) on private roofs (houses, garages, extensions/Anbauten, carports) in the Lippeverband/Ahlen area, at a rate of €50 per m² of greened roof area; both professional (Fachfirma) installation and DIY (Eigenarbeit) execution costs are eligible; can be claimed for one or multiple roofs at the same property address, up to a combined cap of 200 m² / €10,000; applicants wishing to green larger areas beyond this are referred to separate individualised arrangement via hallo@klima-werk.de; source is silent on (i.e. not stated as covered) design/planning, permitting, monitoring, or ongoing maintenance costs

Covers: rainwater cisterns (Regenwasserzisternen), creation/design of rainwater infiltration (Versickerung) areas, and depaving/desealing (Entsiegelung) of concrete or asphalt surfaces on private land -- each eligible for a grant of 30-50% of eligible costs. Exclusions (e.g. green roofs, façade greening, maintenance/monitoring costs) not stated in this source .

Covers: planning/design and construction costs of new green roof or facade systems (substrate, planting, irrigation, retention elements, fall-protection needed for maintenance, extra costs for combination with solar PV) plus mandatory 12-month completion care. Excludes: renovation of existing green roofs/facades, greening required by law/planning permit/building code, green roofs on new buildings, facade insulation/renovation, ongoing/development maintenance (Entwicklungs- und Unterhaltungspflege) beyond the 12 months, decorative garden features, solar thermal/PV equipment itself, official fees (e.g. public-land special-use permits)

Covers: installation/investment costs (materials/construction) of extensive green roof installations (subsidy up to 50% of investment costs, max €25/m², capped at €5,000) and of green façade installations (max €500/building); excludes maintenance, monitoring, and other non-investment costs, which are not mentioned as eligible.

Covers (funded at 50% of total construction/installation costs, capped at €25,000 per person/application per year): green roofs (flat roofs and, newly, pitched roofs), façade greening, and desealing/depaving of home garden and courtyard surfaces. Free architect consultation (Markus Ulmann) is included as a separate non-monetary benefit. Not stated/excluded: rain gardens, rain barrels/cisterns, individual tree planting, ongoing maintenance costs, and separate design/permitting/monitoring costs are not mentioned as covered.

Covers cost of green roof installation (material + labour; DIY or contractor, both eligible) at €50/m², for roofs meeting minimum build standard (10cm substrate or ≥25 L/m² water storage capacity), connected to the sewer system (combined or separate system) and located within the EG/Lippeverband funding catchment area (Fördergebiet); capped at max. 200 m² per property/address (≤€10,000); excludes roofs where greening is already legally mandated (e.g. via Bebauungsplan/Satzung) and projects where work has already started; maintenance costs not mentioned/covered.

Covers: all costs from top of roof waterproofing layer for green roofs (materials, installation, structural reinforcement); planning, material, plant, and 12-month establishment-care costs for façade greening; removal/disposal of sealed surface, soil material, planting, and (for partial desealing) sub-base/paving reconstruction costs; storage tank construction/installation, piping, treatment components, and reinstatement for rain/greywater systems. Excludes: in-kind/self-labour (Eigenleistung) labour costs across all modules; PVC components and their installation; asbestos- or PVC-containing roof coverings (for green roofs); self-clinging climber facade greening, facade renovation, and renovation of existing green facades; decorative finishing work (e.g. painting) for water-reuse systems; chemical-dosing water treatment components

Covers: planning and market-standard costs of building up the vegetation layer/area for roof greening (protective fleece, herbivore protection, filter mats, drainage layer, substrate, seeds/plants) and façade greening (climbing aids/structures, planting beds, seeds/plants), for new-build and existing residential/commercial buildings citywide (min. 10 m² net vegetation area, min. 5 cm root zone depth for roofs). Excludes: VAT where input-tax deductible; works already commissioned/started before approval; measures legally mandated by building/nature-conservation law (e.g. compensation/planning-permission requirements); mere renovation of existing greenery (only the genuinely expanded portion is eligible); installations limited to planters/gravel/paving-decking/decoration/furniture/equipment; photovoltaic or solar-thermal systems; peat-, asbestos- or PVC-containing materials or materials with root inhibitors/biocides or other environmentally harmful materials; and costs whose reasonableness cannot be clearly established.

Covers 50-60% of eligible costs (capped at €20,000 per property) for gärtnerische Gestaltung/greening of courtyards, parking areas and front gardens, plus installation of green roofs and green façades, within the designated Fördergebiet Kapellplatz/Woogsviertel/Ostbahnhof; free advisory consultation and application support also included. Not stated whether design/planning, permitting, maintenance or monitoring costs are separately eligible.

Covers: costs of installing green roofs (materials/substrate/plants, plus labour whether via a specialist firm or DIY/Eigenarbeit) on roof surfaces of carports, extensions, garages and other buildings that are connected to the sewer system (combined or separate) within the EGLV (Emschergenossenschaft/Lippeverband) drainage catchment, which since April 2025 covers essentially all of the Dinslaken municipal area (with a few address-level exceptions); funding is capped at 50 €/m² up to 200 m² per property (max. €10,000). Excludes: roofs outside the drainage catchment area (not connected to the sewer network), roofs where work has already begun before application/approval, and roof greening that is already legally mandated (e.g. as a condition in a Bebauungsplan or municipal statute/Satzung).

Covers: installation costs of green roofs (max €15/m² of designed/greened area, capped at €1,500/measure, and ≤50% of total measure costs), green façades (capped at €500/measure, ≤50% of total measure costs), and PV systems up to 30kWp (flat tiered subsidies: €100 for ≤1kWp, €350 for >1-5kWp, €650 for >5-10kWp, €1,000 for >10-30kWp, also within the general ≤50%-of-costs rule); total programme funding pot capped at €50,000 per round, subject to successful approval (Bewilligung). Excluded/not covered: costs beyond the per-measure caps or beyond 50% of total costs; design/planning, permitting, and monitoring/maintenance costs are not mentioned as covered.

Covered: cost of greening (Begrünung) the roof itself, i.e., materials/installation, via a flat subsidy of €50 per m² of greened roof area, for one or several roofs at the same property/postal address, up to a maximum of 200 m² per property (i.e., up to €10,000); both contractor-installed and DIY/self-installation work are eligible. Excluded/not covered: roofs not connected to the sewer network (Kanalisation) within the Lippeverband catchment; roofs where greening is already legally mandated (e.g., via a Bebauungsplan or Satzung); work already begun before the application is submitted; and areas beyond the 200 m² cap (larger projects are referred to a separate individual arrangement via hallo@klima-werk.de). Not stated as covered: design/permitting, ongoing maintenance, or monitoring costs.

Covers: planning/design costs, installation/construction costs, vegetation-layer materials (protective fleece, filter mat, drainage layer, substrate, seeding/plants), root protection, structural (statics) assessment, façade greening systems and preparatory works (depaving, soil replacement for façade planting), and old-surface disposal costs for depaving. Excludes: VAT if applicant is input-tax-deductible, financing costs, unpaid own labour/in-kind donations, structural/static improvement costs, measures required by building permits/development plans, and planter-box-only measures

Covers: purchase/acquisition, delivery and professional planting costs for up to 3 native deciduous trees per property; material/disposal costs (self-performed) or 80% of invoiced contractor costs for desealing paved/gravel surfaces and naturalistic replanting; planning and installation (professional) or DIY material kit costs for green roofs. Excludes: costs for non-native or non-eligible plant/tree species, works already completed before application/approval (no retroactive funding), and -- for green roofs -- costs beyond the €50/m² or €7,500/project cap.

Covers: material/installation costs for green roof, green façade, courtyard greening, and depaving/greening works; planning, site supervision (Bauleitung) and expert consultancy fees (capped at 10% of eligible costs); shared community amenities (play, path, seating areas + furniture/pergolas, capped at 25% of grant sum); completion-phase care for green roofs; disposal costs for contaminated soil (with invoice proof). Excludes: pure administrative/financing costs, used/second-hand products, general ongoing maintenance (except roof completion care), façade renovation (Fassadensanierung), measures mandated by legal obligation or authority order, elaborate garden features/sculptures/fountains, mere repairs, changes to supply/disposal lines, and costs covered by other public subsidies (no stacking with e.g. KfW/BAFA)

Covers (subordinate to other funding, e.g. BEG, which takes priority): building-envelope security/design measures (roofs, external doors/windows, balconies), shopfront/retail-layout redesign (incl. canopies, floor-plan changes for retail attractiveness), energetic modernisation of windows/doors/façades/roofs tied to an envelope upgrade (incl. insulation between finished/unfinished storeys), structural elements needed to preserve townscape-defining building substance or adapt retail floor plans, barrier-free/low-barrier access measures, and -- as possible additional items -- residential-surroundings design (Wohnumfeldgestaltung) and proportional architect/planning fees (e.g. DIN 276 cost estimate, site supervision/acceptance). Excludes: purely energetic measures without an envelope upgrade (e.g. interior fit-out only); any works/orders placed before the modernisation contract is signed (not retroactively fundable); and costs coverable via other funding sources, since Städtebaufördermittel are explicitly subordinate (nachrangig), with BEG funding to be used first where applicable.

Current regional scheme covers professionally installed extensive roof/façade greening on residential/association buildings; click-system flat roofs may be self-installed; €40/m² up to €1,000; final invoices required.

Covers: physical removal/desealing of impermeable surfaces (pavers, asphalt, concrete) on private/semi-private land and subsequent planting, rewarded with one free native tree or shrub (plus optional planting advice) per registered area ≥5 m²; explicitly excludes cash payment for labour, materials, or ongoing maintenance costs, which are not mentioned as covered
Acquisition, preparation, planning and installation costs for eligible measures; own labour excluded

Covers planning, material and construction costs of: green roofs (from the top of the roof waterproofing) plus durable load-bearing/statics and root-resistance upgrades and 12 months' Fertigstellungspflege; ground- or wall-bound facade greening incl. preparatory works, with 24 months' establishment care (ground-bound) / 12 months (wall-bound); Entsiegelung -- planning, removal and disposal costs plus restoration of natural soil function and subsequent greening (full or partial de-sealing, the latter requiring a greened surface share of at least 25%); and decentralised rainwater retention/infiltration (Versickerungsmulden, Mulden-Rigolen-Systeme, Zisternen, oberirdische Tanksysteme). Bonuses: EUR 300 for planting a site-appropriate, preferably native deciduous tree, EUR 100 for biodiversity-promoting seed (min. 30 species over min. 15 m²). Own-labour installation: material costs only, invoices required -- labour hours not eligible. NOT covered: full-surface paving even where the pavers are water-permeable; timber decking and wood paving; furniture, play equipment and elaborate ornamental garden installations; standard commercial water butts (Regentonnen); gutters and downpipes themselves; renovation of existing facade greening; a structural engineer's suitability assessment unless the greening is then carried out. Grant capped at 60% of eligible costs, max EUR 15,000 per property.

Covers, at the applicable Fördersatz: plants/trees, materials (Pflanzpfahl, Strick, Substrat; Dachvorbereitung, Drän- und Speicherschichten; Rankhilfen, Durchwurzelungsschutz; Oberboden; gebietseigene Saatgutmischungen) and Arbeitskosten; for Entsiegelung also Entsorgungskosten; for Baumpflege the Kronenpflege-/Kronenregenerationsschnitte, Kronensicherungs-/Stabilisierungssysteme, Baumumfeldverbesserung and Totholzentfernung only in connection with such work. Excludes: Pflegekosten for every measure; tree-care jobs under €500 (Bagatellgrenze); Verkehrssicherungsmaßnahmen; removal of leaves/fallen deadwood; Formschnitte; and any measure required by öffentlich-rechtliche Verpflichtung (Baumschutzverordnung, BNatSchG, BayNatSchG, BayKompV, Stellplatzsatzung, Ersatzaufforstungen, Pflanzgebote nach Bebauungsplan).

Covers: construction/installation costs for green roofs (≥15m², 15€/m² up to 50% costs, max €3,000), green façades (50% of costs, max €2,500), and depaving/desealing (≥5m², €250 flat + €30/m² thereafter, max €3,000); material costs also eligible if self-installed (Eigenleistung). Excludes: costs from installations completed more than 12 months prior; no explicit coverage of design/permitting/monitoring/ongoing maintenance for this specific programme

Covered: unsealing/depaving of front gardens and courtyards (with removal/disposal of sealed surfaces), planting of perennials/shrubs/trees, pergolas (wood)/climbing aids/greened entrance archways, ground-bound greening of walls, fences and bin enclosures, installation of topsoil/planting substrate for permanent planting, ground-bound facade greening (incl. removal of sealed surfaces), seeding of extensive lawn mixes/wildflower meadows and perennials, extensive and intensive green roofs, and "green" parking surfaces using greenable surface paving systems (grass grid pavers) incl. substructure and substrate. Excluded: structures such as carports and garden sheds; technical installations and infrastructure facilities; decorative elements (e.g. fountains, sculptures); movable garden furniture (e.g. planters); installation of paving (including eco-paving); and own labour (Eigenleistungen).
Materials and contracted installation required for the measure; own labour costs excluded; ongoing care excluded; permits only where required, with no express permit-cost reimbursement

Covers the total investment leading to a new green roof/façade, including roof construction, sealing, substrate and plants; 50%, maximum €2,000; minimum investment €1,000. Maintenance, planning, permits and monitoring: Not stated. Compliance remains applicant responsibility.
