Covers: full construction cost of private-lot rainwater infiltration facilities (up to ¥200,000) and 50% of purchase price (incl. delivery, installation, tax) of 100-1,000L rain storage tanks (up to ¥100,000). Excludes: properties held by real-estate/construction businesses for resale, sites without landowner consent, applicants with unpaid municipal taxes, sites subject to certain development/land-reshaping regulations (for infiltration facilities only), and any costs exceeding the caps (self-funded).

Covers part of the eligible construction/installation cost (per standardized unit cost schedule set by the ward) of private-lot rainwater infiltration facilities (雨水浸透ます/雨水浸透施設) that let roof runoff infiltrate the ground, up to ¥400,000; excludes: (1) sites in the designated landfill districts (Heiwajima, Showajima, Tokai, Keihinjima, Haneda Airport area, etc.) and, even within the eligible area, zones with steep-slope safety risk, slope-face instability risk, environmental harm risk, or high groundwater (within ~1m of surface); (2) facilities owned by the ward, national/local government or public corporations/equivalent bodies, or buildings subject to Ōta's development guidance ordinance (開発指導要綱); applicant must be the facility/site owner or rights-holder and not delinquent on resident/corporate tax. No coverage of maintenance/monitoring costs or other NbS types is indicated in this source.

Covers: purchase cost of the rain barrel/tank unit and its accessories (tank scheme), and construction cost of installing infiltration inlets (ます scheme), each at 2/3 reimbursement up to size-based caps. Excludes: design/planning fees, permitting fees, ongoing maintenance costs, and monitoring costs (not listed as eligible). Excludes buildings intended for sale or exhibition. Requires up-to-date payment of sewerage usage fee/beneficiary charge in sewerage-plan areas, and infiltration inlet work must use a City-designated contractor.

Covers: purchase and installation cost (partial) of rainwater storage tanks (雨水貯留タンク) for residents, aimed at effective rainwater use and securing emergency water in disasters. Excludes/not stated: green infrastructure (roofs, façades, rain gardens, permeable paving, trees), maintenance costs, design/planning, permitting, monitoring costs.

Covers 1/2 of construction costs for new rainwater storage tank installation (≥100L, fixed, connected to gutters, cleanable) or for converting an existing septic tank (made redundant by sewer connection or new septic install) into a rainwater storage facility, for residences (incl. small mixed-use shops with ≥1/2 floor area residential); excludes work begun before grant approval and is capped/budget-limited.

Covers: installation/construction costs (設置工事費, or purchase cost if self-installed) for rainwater storage tanks (貯留タンク, ≥100L, max 1/site) and infiltration facilities (浸透ます, ≥25cm internal diameter, ≥50cm depth, max 4/site), subsidy calculated as the lower of a per-unit/volume rate or actual installation/purchase cost, capped per facility type (¥50,000 for storage tanks, ¥100,000 if converting from a septic tank, ¥100,000 for infiltration facilities, ¥100,000 combined cap if installing both). Excludes: costs where the facility was already purchased/installed prior to approval/application; where the applicant is delinquent on municipal taxes; where the facility receives rainwater inflow from sources other than the roof; where a similar facility on the same site has already received this subsidy; where installation is undertaken pursuant to consultation/procedures under Sakura City's Development Project Procedures and Standards Ordinance (開発事業の手続及び基準に関する条例); and where the storage facility is a converted single-treatment septic tank that already received a separate city subsidy for conversion to a combined-treatment septic tank.

Covers: (1) conversion work cost of repurposing a disused septic tank into a rainwater storage facility (改造工事; flat JPY35,000/case), including incidental works within the scope of tank-installation work (e.g. height-adjustment blocks per FAQ); and (2) purchase and installation cost of new commercial rainwater storage tanks (1/2 of cost, up to JPY20,000/unit, max 2 units per building). Excludes: portions paid via points/coupons; purchases made before the grant decision notice is received; buildings held for resale purposes; and buildings owned by national/local government or equivalent public bodies.

Covers: half of installation/construction costs (工事費) for rain barrel/cistern (≥100L airtight container) or infiltration pit (≥30cm diameter) at owner-occupied residences within Sayama City. Excludes: costs above the 1/2 share, amounts beyond the ¥30,000/¥40,000 caps, and any maintenance, monitoring, design or permitting costs (not mentioned as covered). Infiltration facility not permitted on cliff-adjacent or high-groundwater sites.

Covers: 1/2 of planting/installation costs (植栽費用) for eligible green infrastructure (rooftop greening, wall/façade greening, roadside-frontage tree greening, rain gardens, indoor greening), within designated priority green districts (緑化重点地区), subject to caps (JPY 5 million total, JPY 500,000 for roadside greening, up to JPY 10 million for high-quality greening in the central priority district). Excludes: areas subject to mandatory greening under the Mori no Miyako (杜の都の環境をつくる条例) ordinance; areas already certified under a greening plan by FY2022; for-profit building-sale projects; areas already receiving another subsidy; design/permitting/monitoring and maintenance costs are not mentioned as covered.

Covers: 2/3 of installation/construction cost for rainwater storage facilities (雨水貯留施設, e.g. 天水桶 rain barrels/cisterns) and rainwater infiltration facilities (雨水浸透施設: 浸透ます infiltration manholes, 浸透トレンチ infiltration trenches), up to a ¥50,000 limit, installed by the owner-occupant at their own existing home in the city. Excludes: new-build/rebuild (新築・建替え) installations; facilities at homes not yet 1+ year post-construction; developments already subject to the city's land development/mid-high-rise building guidance ordinance (指導要綱); and any facility for which the applicant has already received this subsidy before or is eligible for an equivalent subsidy under another program.

Covers a portion of the installation cost of rainwater infiltration inlets (雨水浸透ます) for residential sites and small (<1,000㎡) multi-unit residential/office/commercial sites within urban planning areas (excluding landslide-designated zones): up to ¥30,000 per unit, capped at 2 units (roof area <160㎡) or 4 units (roof area ≥160㎡). Excludes (not mentioned as covered): design/planning costs, permitting costs, monitoring, and ongoing maintenance; applicant must pay upfront and is reimbursed after post-installation inspection. Not covered/mentioned: rainwater storage tanks/barrels, green infrastructure (green roofs/façades, rain gardens), permeable paving, or tree planting.

Covers: construction/installation costs (工事費等経費) for setting up a commercial rainwater storage tank, or for converting a septic tank (made unnecessary by sewer connection) into a rainwater storage facility, within the city, subject to a subsidy of 1/2 of costs up to a ¥50,000 cap; if self-installed without a contractor, only the purchase cost of the tank body and necessary installation parts is eligible (tools excluded). Excludes: tools; any self-install costs beyond tank/parts; costs exceeding the approved estimate/grant decision amount; and (not mentioned in source, so inferred as excluded per standard scheme structure) design/planning fees, permitting fees, ongoing maintenance and monitoring costs.

Covers (per-measure, each capped, once per building/unit): (1) Septic-tank-conversion rainwater storage tank installation/construction work costs -- 1/2 of construction cost, cap ¥50,000; (2) Simple/prefabricated rainwater storage tank material costs -- 1/2 of material cost, cap ¥20,000 (<500L), ¥35,000 (500-1000L), or ¥50,000 (≥1000L); (3) Rainwater infiltration masu (soakaway) construction costs -- Type A (with perforated pipe): full cost, cap ¥15,000; Type B (without): full cost, cap ¥10,000, up to 2 units per building. Excludes: applicants with unpaid municipal taxes; tanks/facilities installed in newly-built for-sale (建売) housing; work/material purchase begun before application approval/decision; buildings that have previously received this subsidy; and (implicitly, not itemized as a coverage line) ongoing maintenance/inspection costs, which remain the owner's responsibility.

Covers: cost of purchasing the rainwater storage tank itself (product price incl. consumption tax), 2/3 of price or ¥200/L whichever lower, up to ¥40,000. Excludes: installation costs (設置費), delivery/shipping costs (配送費等), and any ongoing maintenance/repair costs.

Covers: purchase cost of small rainwater tanks (100L-<1,000L); construction/installation cost of mid/large storage tanks/cisterns with pumps and piping (≥1,000L); conversion cost of decommissioned septic tanks into rainwater storage; construction cost of rainwater infiltration pits/trenches. Excludes: fire-water storage tanks (防火水槽) specifically excluded from mid/large grant; drinking-water use is prohibited (use limited to toilet flushing/watering); national and local government entities excluded from eligibility; taxes owed applicants excluded (must have no delinquent municipal tax).

Covers a portion (2/3, capped) of the purchase/installation cost of a rainwater storage tank (≥100L) fed via a simple gutter-collection fixture; excludes ongoing maintenance costs; requires no municipal tax arrears and a signed maintenance agreement.

Covers: partial cost of purchase (materials) and installation/construction work for a new rainwater storage tank (≥100L capacity, non-electric, meeting design standards), up to 1/2 of combined cost capped at ¥30,000, one tank per detached house (up to 2 for multi-unit buildings), one-time grant only. Excludes: already-installed tanks, design/planning fees, permitting, ongoing maintenance, monitoring, and any tank not meeting the structural criteria (light-blocking material, cleanable, stable, pest-proof lid/filter, overflow protection).

Covers: installation/construction cost of rainwater storage tank (≥200L) or infiltration facility (≥300mm diameter infiltration boxes, 3+ units), including material costs if self-installed (materials, piping, labor as itemized in submitted receipts/estimates). Excludes: septic tank conversions already covered under the separate 合併処理浄化槽事業補助金 (joint treatment septic tank subsidy); limited to one application per residence; requires prior-year completion and invoice submission by deadline.

Covers: 1/2 of the material cost and installation/construction (施工) cost of the rain tank (雨水タンク, ≥150L, market or self-made, max 1/site) or infiltration facility (浸透ます, ≥30cm dia., concrete/resin with lid, market product, max 4/site) itself, up to fixed caps (¥30,000 for tanks / ¥50,000 for infiltration facilities, rounded down below ¥1,000); for storage tanks this extends to fittings/gutter processing (継手部品・雨どい加工). Excludes: surrounding fences/platforms or stands not bundled with the product (unless sold as an inseparable set); any installation completed before grant approval/prior to application (must apply before construction begins); and (per eligibility rules) applicants with arrears on municipal taxes, water, sewerage, or agricultural settlement drainage fees are ineligible.

Covered: free supply of infiltration-well materials only -- the rainwater infiltration inlet unit (雨水浸透ます, concrete or polypropylene), No.4 crushed stone (4号砕石), and permeable filter sheet (透水シート) -- for residential buildings, parking lots and similar land citywide (excluding development-permit-subject properties and private roads). Excluded: installation/construction labour cost, which must be performed by a city-designated drainage equipment contractor (指定工事店) and is fully self-funded by the applicant; sites unsuitable for infiltration (e.g. steep slopes) are ineligible; ongoing maintenance (annual debris/clog removal) is the owner's responsibility.

Covers 1/2 of the installation/construction cost (設置工事に要する額) for rainwater infiltration facilities (infiltration manholes/masu 浸透桝 and buried infiltration pipes 浸透地下埋設管) meeting the required type/quantity per site-area tier, up to tiered subsidy caps of ¥35,000-¥150,000 depending on lot size. Excludes design/planning, permitting, maintenance, and monitoring costs (not mentioned as covered). Eligibility restricted to individuals installing facilities within designated urbanization-promotion zones (市街化区域), excluding steep-slope collapse hazard zones, high-groundwater areas, and other areas deemed unsuitable for infiltration facilities.

Covers: planting materials and labor costs; planting-base materials (soil amendment, rooftop/wall/parking greening substrates); irrigation facilities (sprinkler taps, supply/drainage pipes) for green roofs, green walls, open-space/garden greening, parking-lot greening, and hedges. Excludes: works for commercial promotion of greening methods/materials (営業を目的とした緑化事業); projects under 50m² (for general greening work) or hedges under 15m; herbaceous annual/biennial plants that die within 2 years (１、２年草); work not completed by March 15 of the application fiscal year.

Covers: purchase cost and installation/construction work cost of an above-ground rainwater storage tank (≥100L capacity, durable, unused/new product, 1 unit per household). Excludes: tanks purchased before grant approval, tanks below 100L, more than 1 unit per household, and applicants with unpaid municipal taxes or sewerage beneficiary charges/apportionments; limited to individuals (not corporations) at their residence or planned residence

Covers: half (1/2, rounded down below ¥1,000) of the installation/construction cost for (a) rainwater storage tanks (100L+) and infiltration facilities (infiltration inlets/浸透ます, infiltration trenches, infiltration side ditches, permeable paving) under the rainwater storage/infiltration facility subsidy, subject to a ¥200,000 per-application cap and per-facility sub-caps (e.g., ¥30,000-60,000 for tanks, ¥8,000/unit or /m for infiltration works, ¥1,000/m² for permeable paving); and (b) separately, half of the cost (capped at ¥60,000) of septic-tank-to-rainwater-storage conversion works, specifically pump-out/cleaning of the tank, removal of unneeded internal parts and partition drilling, rainwater drainpipe installation, and pump/sill-cock (garden tap) installation. Excludes: costs incurred before submitting the application/before approval (no retroactive or post-construction claims accepted), ongoing 7-year maintenance costs (upkeep is the applicant's own responsibility per the pledge form), and any costs beyond the per-application or per-facility caps; design, permitting, and monitoring costs are not mentioned as covered.

Three schemes, each with distinct covered/excluded costs: (1) Rain barrel/cistern tank subsidy -- covers the tank unit purchase price and installation work cost (≥80L commercially sold tank, must be purchased/installed via a Tsu City-based business); excludes tanks <80L or purchased/installed outside the city, and excludes ongoing maintenance (not itemized as covered). (2) Jōkasō-to-rainwater-storage conversion subsidy -- covers conversion work only: interior cleaning/removal of unneeded items inside the decommissioned tank, downspout-to-tank piping work, and pump/hose-bib installation work, performed by a city-designated sewer-works contractor; excludes tank purchase (existing septic tank is reused, not bought) and requires no arrears in municipal tax/sewer beneficiary charges/sewer usage fees; excludes work begun before approval. (3) Jōkasō installation subsidy (general sanitation programme, src_315_2) -- covers new-build or conversion installation cost of the jōkasō tank itself, plus separate itemized caps for full removal of an old single-treatment tank or pit latrine, conversion-for-reuse-as-rainwater-storage work, and piping costs, tiered by tank person-capacity; excludes work begun before approval, and post-installation the owner is responsible for statutory maintenance/inspection/cleaning (not a covered cost).

Covered: 1/2 of purchase cost of the rainwater storage tank plus its standard accessories/mounting frame and installation/construction cost (for new installations), or the conversion work cost plus fixed pump cost (for septic-tank conversions); also self-build material costs; fixed pump cost included for underground-tank systems. Subsidy capped at ¥30,000 for tanks 100-500L and ¥50,000 for tanks ≥500L, with amounts under ¥1,000 rounded down. Excluded: hose/nozzle at the tap end, separately-sold accessories, and watering-purpose pumps. Limit of one unit per building (household), must be installed/completed within the same fiscal year as application (no cross-fiscal-year disbursement), and applicant must have no outstanding municipal tax arrears.

Covers: purchase cost of the rainwater tank itself plus purchase of accessory fittings needed to connect the tank to the downspout/gutter branch. Excludes: installation labor, transport, handling/other fees, and the cost of a stand/platform (架台) for the tank.

Covers: installation cost of rainwater infiltration facilities (infiltration catch basins/masu and infiltration trenches, meeting specified technical standards) at existing single-family homes (including mixed residential-commercial use) within the city, up to one-half of installation cost or ¥50,000, whichever is less, limited to once per household. Excludes: facilities at houses owned by corporations/businesses; facilities installed to satisfy Machizukuri Ordinance Art. 37/48 mandatory requirements; sites unsuitable per the Saitama Prefecture infiltration-capacity map, steep-slope sites, or sites where infiltration would compromise slope/retaining-wall safety or cause groundwater contamination/environmental damage; maintenance costs (owner must maintain facility, but maintenance itself is not a covered/reimbursed cost) ; design/permitting costs not mentioned as covered . Rain storage tank (雨水貯留槽) installation is covered under a separate, distinct subsidy scheme referenced on the parent page but not detailed in this source .

Covers: cost of installing infiltration wells (雨水浸透ます Type A/B, capped at ¥100,000/unit and ¥50,000/unit respectively, full subsidy up to cap) and rainwater storage tanks (雨水貯留タンク, total capacity ≥200L, capped at ¥30,000/building, full subsidy up to cap), on residential/office/shop buildings with gutters ("住宅等"), limited to the number of units allowed per building floor area (1 unit if <50㎡, 2 units if ≥50㎡, for infiltration wells). Excludes: costs exceeding the caps; infiltration wells (not tanks) in designated hazard zones (砂防指定地, 地すべり防止区域, 急傾斜地崩壊危険区域, and other slope-stability risk zones) -- no such zone exclusion applies to storage tanks; installations required under the city's development permit guidance standards (焼津市開発許可指導基準); remodeling/repair/re-installation of a facility previously subsidized under this scheme; applicants already receiving similar subsidies from the national government or other local governments; and installation begun before grant approval. Ongoing maintenance/upkeep costs after installation are explicitly borne by the recipient, not covered.

Covers a portion of material/unit costs and construction/installation costs for three facility types: (1) rainwater storage tanks (雨水貯留槽) -- material cost of tank unit incl. connecting pipe but excl. stand/platform (架台); installation cost incl. tank unit + connecting pipe + earthwork + drainage pump if needed; (2) septic-tank conversion to storage (浄化槽等改造) -- construction cost incl. partition-wall drilling etc. and drainage pump if needed, but excluding cleaning/disinfection costs; (3) rainwater infiltration basins (雨水浸透ます) -- material cost of unit incl. lid, non-woven fabric, crushed stone; installation cost incl. same items plus earthwork. Overall: excludes septic-tank cleaning/disinfection costs and storage-tank stand/platform (架台) costs. Subsidy amount is calculated tax-inclusive with amounts under ¥1,000 rounded down.

Covers: (1) installation of a commercial rainwater storage tank/barrel on a building with habitable rooms in Yashio City -- up to 2/3 of cost, capped at ¥30,000 per unit; or (2) conversion of an existing septic tank (single or combined type) into a rainwater storage facility -- flat ¥80,000. Excludes/conditions: applicant must own the building (with habitable rooms), be current on municipal tax payment (no unpaid tax) and be subject to municipal tax (non-taxable persons are ineligible for the subsidy); excludes repeat funding for a facility that already received this subsidy previously; requires a 7-year maintenance/management agreement with the city (ongoing maintenance itself not funded); tank accessories (e.g., hoses) may be sold separately and are not necessarily covered; does not cover design, permitting, or monitoring costs.

Covers 3/4 of the purchase cost (incl. shipping and consumption tax) of the rainwater storage tank body plus accessories (e.g., stand/frame), capped at ¥45,000 (amounts under ¥1,000 rounded down); excludes installation/construction work costs and any other miscellaneous costs. Eligible tanks must be newly installed (not already installed), have capacity ≥100L, not be for display/resale, and be limited to max 2 units per building (5-year replacement exception applies once 2 units are already installed); only tanks purchased after application acceptance qualify.

Covers: part of the construction/implementation cost of ground, rooftop, and wall/facade greening that exceeds statutory (法令等で定める基準) minimum greening standards, for citizens/businesses greening publicly-accessible private land in high-footfall areas such as station-front and city-center locations. Excludes: sites in urbanization-control zones (市街化調整区域); ongoing/post-installation maintenance costs are not stated as covered -- only a maintenance-status report (維持管理状況報告書) is required after the grant .

Covers: full installation cost (設置費用の全額) of new rainwater storage tanks (up to ¥30,000/unit, max 1 unit) and new rainwater infiltration pits/soakaways (up to ¥30,000/unit, max 4 units), for those newly installing such equipment within Yonezawa City's urbanization-promotion area (市街化区域内). Excludes : maintenance/monitoring costs, design/planning and permitting costs, installations outside the urbanization-promotion area, existing (non-new) installations, and any costs beyond the per-unit caps -- none of these are mentioned as covered.

Covers subsidy for installation costs of: rainwater infiltration inlets (雨水浸透ます, ≥2 per site), infiltration trenches connected to inlets (雨水浸透トレンチ, ≥1m), permeable asphalt paving of parking lots ≥100㎡ (浸透性アスファルト舗装), and rainwater storage tanks connected to a downspout that drains to infiltration (雨水貯留槽, subsidy = 1/2 of unit price before tax). Excludes: cases falling under Article 3 of the Zama City Development Business Guidance Guidelines (座間市開発等事業指導要綱第3条) except storage tanks; installations for purposes of real-estate sale/development; applicants delinquent on municipal tax; and any construction begun before application approval. Not stated: ongoing maintenance/cleaning costs are not addressed as an explicit coverage exclusion in this source (a related but separate page discusses cleaning of infiltration inlets).

Covers up to 90% of rainwater storage tank (rainwater-use facility) installation cost, with exact maximum cap set by annual public notice; does not cover ongoing operation/maintenance costs -- owner must operate and maintain the facility per submitted maintenance plan, subject to full or partial subsidy clawback if not operated without justification, improperly installed/defective construction, or improvement recommendations not followed. Broader LID/water-cycle infrastructure works (src_327_2) are a separate public-infrastructure programme, not part of this household grant's coverage.

Covers construction/installation costs of rooftop gardens (up to 70% for private buildings; fully city-funded for public buildings); excludes explicit mention of design, permitting, monitoring, or ongoing maintenance funding. Structural safety assessment and public-access/maintenance agreement are prerequisites but not stated as separately funded cost items.

Covers: professional consultancy fees, administrative/permit/legal fees, project management (up to 50%), construction/labour, supplies and materials (plants, soil, irrigation, waterproofing, structures, planters), maintenance for 3 years (up to 30%). Excludes: tools, PPE, travel and structural renovation
Covers system equipment and installation; no evidence that permitting, design, monitoring or subsequent maintenance costs are covered

Covers: newly installed green roofs (min. 30 L/m² water storage capacity) and downspout/roof disconnection projects (fully disconnecting roof rainwater from combined or improved-separated sewer, combined with rainwater storage, a wadi, or underground infiltration facility), reimbursed up to per-m² rates and caps, never exceeding actual incurred costs. Excludes: existing green roofs, roof maintenance, roof replacement, and partial disconnection (overflow to sewer not allowed); applicant bears responsibility for structural load-bearing capacity and effective on-site rainwater processing.

Covers: material and (where applicable) installation costs for green/blue/green-blue roofs, structural reinforcement to bear a blue roof's water load, disconnection of paved surfaces from the sewer (per-area/per-volume flat amounts, up to 100% of costs), and rainwater harvesting/storage systems (20% of material+installation). Excludes: drinking-quality use of harvested rainwater, costs already covered by other subsidies beyond 100% of total cost, and (implicitly) ongoing maintenance and permit fees, which are not listed as eligible cost types.

Covers: fixed per-unit/per-m² subsidy amounts toward materials/installation costs for ten defined green/blue measures on private property (green roof, rain barrel, waterschutting rain-fence, depaving/greening, water-permeating paving, water-permeable paving, tree planting, white roof coating, underground infiltration facility, underground water tank), available to residents, renters (with landlord consent required for green roof, waterschutting, underground infiltration/tank, and white roof), and businesses/institutions (at separate, generally higher rates/caps). Excludes: new-build and full renovation projects carried out entirely by a project developer or contractor; excludes ongoing maintenance costs (e.g. extra upkeep of a green roof is the owner's responsibility); no coverage of design/planning, permitting, or monitoring costs ; max 1 application per address per year, subject to annual budget ("op=op").

Covers: purchase of materials and cost of having measures carried out (labour+materials) for green roofs, tile removal/depaving, water storage/rain buffers, and rain barrels; includes roof load-bearing advice (max €200, only if project executed) if applicable. Excludes: self-performed labour (DIY work), permit costs, maintenance costs, and replacement of previously subsidised measures.

Covers: cost of green roof materials only (sedum or biodiverse roof system), scaled by roof type and water-retention capacity (€20-€40/m²), minimum 6 m² greened, roof must retain ≥15 L/m². Excludes: advisory/design costs and installation/labour costs, which are explicitly not reimbursed
Installation of green roofs/façades/vertical gardens; structural calculation up to €250; existing buildings only; design, permitting and monitoring not stated

Green roofs: 50% of directly necessary realisation costs; refundable VAT and permit fees excluded. Valuable vegetation: necessary direct research, advice and preservation costs. Depaving: €15/m² rather than documented cost categories. Actual payment cannot exceed realised costs.

Covers: costs of physically disconnecting the roof downspout from the combined sewer and constructing the rainwater storage/infiltration provision (above- or below-ground; min. 30 m² roof disconnected; min. ~20 L storage per m² disconnected roof); for roofs ≤250m² a fixed rate (€7/m² above-ground or €14/m² below-ground); for roofs >250m² actual invoiced costs up to the same per-m² caps; disconnection onto private surface water (ditch/gully/pond) also covered at actual cost, and disconnection onto public road/wadi covered at actual cost only if sufficient account has been taken of private-surface disconnection. Excludes: purchase of a rain barrel itself (only eligible as part of the required overall storage/disconnection provision, not separately subsidised); ongoing maintenance; works started before approval (prior approval required); buildings built in 2011 or later (already required to be disconnected) and properties outside combined-sewer areas.

Covers 30-65% of direct costs of green-blue measures (green roofs/façades, downspout disconnection with rain barrels, communal/edible gardens, depaving of hardened surfaces, tree planting, etc.) on existing (pre-2020) buildings/plots within Arnhem's built-up area (bebouwde kom); subsidy rate within the 30-65% range varies by measure type and location, with higher rates in designated focus areas (urban heat areas, Arnhem-Oost districts of Klarendal, Geitenkamp, Presikhaaf-West, Malburgen, Arnhemse Broek, and Lombok); excludes new-build construction, except rain barrel requests which are exempt from the pre-2020 condition; costs must be substantiated by a quote; max €5,000 per application for individual residents and max €25,000 for collaborations/businesses/institutions/property owners.

Covers: purchase/installation materials and labour for green roofs (incl. structural inspection costs), rainwater storage/infiltration facilities, downspout disconnection, semi-permeable paving (material+installation+removal of old tiles), depaving/greening (plants, potting soil, disposal, gardener costs), façade gardens (native plants, soil, gardener costs, climbing aids). Excludes: measures in public space, roof renovation itself, ongoing maintenance after installation, and (for several measures) buildings constructed after 2012

Eligible scope includes measure-specific materials/plants and installation, structural study where applicable, depaving/soil/planting and rainwater facilities; exclusions include roof covering/replacement and structural alterations where specified; green-schoolyard grants earmark €2,500 for maintenance.

Eligible scope includes green-roof/façade design, installation, materials/plants and non-recoverable VAT; green-boundary materials/plants; depaving plants/shrubs/trees/grass; and shading devices. Maintenance/repair/replacement are excluded; labour is generally excluded except where expressly allowed.

Covers: subsidised group-purchase price of rain barrels/green roof products including delivery, base/stand, and installation assistance (installation only available within Delft); free personal advice on suitable product/design; FAQ/helpdesk support; coordination support for collective street/neighbourhood greening actions. Excludes: no evidence of direct cash grants, tax rebates, loans, or ongoing maintenance funding -- resident bears the (discounted) purchase cost itself.

Covers a fixed per-unit/per-m² subsidy amount toward the specific climate-adaptive measure taken (e.g. €25/€50 per rain barrel/cistern, €5/m² depaving+greening, €35 per tree, €60 up to €25,000 for downspout/sewer disconnection, €20/m² up to €2,000 for green roof, €30/m² up to €2,500 for green façade, €50 per address for façade garden, €20/m per boundary greening up to €500, €100/m³ up to €1,000 for rainwater-use installation), paid on presentation of a receipt/invoice and before-and-after photos as proof of the measure carried out; a 25% bonus is added when ≥3 neighbours jointly carry out the same measure. Excluded: design/planning costs, ongoing maintenance and monitoring costs, and permit fees themselves -- permits ("eventuele vergunningen") are listed only as a required supporting document to submit with the application, not as a reimbursed cost item (not stated as covered).

Covers: (1) green roof installation, minimum 5 m², at up to €25/m² subsidy; (2) downspout/roof disconnection from the sewer, minimum 10 m² disconnected, conditional on following advice from an 'afkoppelcoach' (specific amount/scope of this subsidy not detailed in source). Excludes/not mentioned: design, permitting, monitoring, or ongoing maintenance costs for either measure; also explicitly excludes maintenance of adopted public play/green spaces ('initiatiefplekken'), which residents must maintain themselves -- this exclusion applies to a related but distinct neighbourhood-redesign scheme, not to the two named subsidy measures themselves.

Covers: material/installation costs for the 3 eligible measures on a privately-owned building/plot ≥5 years old, works carried out from 1 Jan 2019 onward -- (1) depaving+living-green replacement (min. 20 m², €5/m², max €2,500); (2) green roof with proven water-retention norm of 30L/m² (min. 10 m², €25/m², max €25,000); (3) sewer disconnection with an additional infiltration provision beyond a rain barrel alone (min. 20 m², min. 20L/m² capture, €10/m², max €10,000). Excludes: artificial grass (kunstgras), gravel/other semi-permeable paving (grind/halfverharding), a rain barrel alone without extra infiltration solution, rental tenants (owner-only), works predating 1 Jan 2019, and prior-subsidised works on the same measure; green roof and sewer disconnection cannot be combined (both address water storage).

Measure-based contribution toward installation; excludes post-1 January 2022 new-build projects and vacant land; measures below technical thresholds are ineligible; permits and owner consent remain applicant responsibilities

Covers: installation/construction (aanleg) of extensive, intensive or blue green roofs including materials and labour per m²; optional structural load-bearing assessment fee (up to €250, or €125 if found unsuitable). Excludes: ongoing maintenance, and roofs on buildings younger than 2 years; joint/neighbour applications get +10% bonus subsidy within same caps. Rain barrel scheme covers reimbursement toward purchase of 1-2 barrels (amount not stated in these sources).

Measure-based contribution toward installation; excludes post-1 January 2022 new-build projects and vacant land; measures below technical thresholds are ineligible; permits and owner consent remain applicant responsibilities

Covers: (1) green roof -- purchase/installation (offerte) costs of a qualifying green roof on an existing roof (min. 20 m², min. 30 L/m² water retention, subsidy up to €25/m² or €35/m² if extra criteria met, max 50% of total cost); (2) rain barrel -- purchase and (if applicable) connection costs of a rain barrel (min. 150 L, placed on own property), max 50% of costs, only combinable with or conditional on the green roof subsidy (or prior green-roof subsidy/self-funded green roof). Excluded/limited: works already started before application are not eligible; total public support (this subsidy plus any other subsidies/contributions received) may never exceed the actual cost of the roof/rain barrel; ongoing maintenance/upkeep costs are not covered, and the green roof must remain in good condition for at least 5 years or the subsidy can be (partly) reclaimed.

Covers one-off investment/execution costs of the specific green measure taken -- labour, materials, and VAT tied to installation/execution -- reimbursed per the stated per-measure rate/cap and never exceeding the amount the applicant actually paid; claims must be submitted within 6 months of execution with photos and invoices as evidence. Excluded: first-time garden/terrain construction (measure 4 only), any amount above what the applicant actually paid, ongoing maintenance/upkeep of the measure (applicant's own responsibility), re-claiming subsidy for a measure already granted at the same address/for that address, and combining more than one measure's subsidy on a single purchase (also measure 1 and measure 3 cannot be combined with each other).

Covers: installation of green roofs (extensive/intensive with min. water storage 25/50 l/m²), green facades, and vertical gardens on private homes/buildings within Heerlen; also free in-kind geveltuintje (tile-to-plant facade garden). Excludes: green roofs on 'bijgebouwen' (outbuildings/sheds); no coverage confirmed for design, monitoring, or ongoing maintenance costs; permit costs not confirmed as covered.
Green-roof contractor/supplier work or material purchases; disconnection materials, contractor/supplier costs and equipment hire; green-roof support cannot exceed actual costs

Covers only material costs (materiaalkosten) of installing a green/sedum roof on a house, garage, or shed (flat or sloped roofs) at €20/m² up to €2,000/address; excludes labour and any other costs (only material costs are stated eligible), and excludes work/installation started before approval (retroactive applications are rejected -- "Achteraf aanvragen kan niet"); no explicit mention of coverage for design, permitting, maintenance, or monitoring costs.

Covers: municipal payment of costs to disconnect large private roofs from the combined sewer system; free provision of infiltration crates for on-site rainwater infiltration; integration of rainwater separation infrastructure into scheduled road/sewer works. Excludes: no stated coverage of green roof, green façade, rain garden, permeable paving, or tree-planting installation/purchase costs; no explicit maintenance funding for resident-installed measures; general water-capture measures (rain barrels, façade gardens, green roofs) are only referenced as resident actions or supported via a separate external water-board (AGV) subsidy, not by Hilversum's own budget

Covers: 50% of documented materials and installation/construction costs for green roofs (max €10,000), blue-green roofs (max €12,500), garden greening/depaving (€10/m² up to €5,000, capped at actual green-product costs), rainwater use installations (max €2,500 residential/€10,000 non-residential), and water recycling systems (max €2,000 residential/€5,000 non-residential); plus a separate reimbursement up to €200 for a structural roof calculation if required (green/blue-green roof only); plus a flat €25 point-of-sale discount per rain barrel (max 2). Excludes: ongoing maintenance costs, connection to drinking-water mains (rainwater/recycling installations), and any costs beyond the stated per-measure caps or beyond actual invoiced/documented costs; design/permitting/monitoring costs are not mentioned as covered.

Covers: material costs, labour costs, and turnover tax (VAT/omzetbelasting) for installation of the specific rainwater measure (rain barrel/water column, water screen, infiltration facility, wadi/rainwater pond ≥100L) or green roof (≥6m², water storage ≥25L/m²). Excludes: facade/roof construction adaptation, administrative costs, and permit costs; for green roofs, additionally excludes gravel, leaf catcher, separation profile, transport costs and other ancillary installation costs. Rain barrel/water column only eligible in combination with another qualifying measure (wadi, water screen, infiltration facility, green roof, or green façade).
Covers a percentage of documented “voorzieningenkosten” for the listed measures, subject to caps and technical conditions. Exclusions beyond those expressly stated: Not stated.

Covers: material and labour costs for depaving/greening (tile/paving removal + planting), green roof construction (waterproofing/drainage/substrate/vegetation layers), and rainwater storage/infiltration devices (rain barrels, columns, gravel boxes, wadis). Excludes: public/street pavement adjustments (e.g. façade gardens on public land), structural/constructive costs (new roof construction, adaptations to roof structures, canopies, fences, pergolas, wall blocks), gravel or non-green materials without rooting capacity, artificial turf, and rain barrels under 300L purchased standalone (must combine with another measure).

Covers: green roof installation (min. 30l/m² water storage) and roof/downspout disconnection measures (to unpaved vegetated terrain, with rain barrel/rainwater storage ≥100l, or with an infiltration facility such as a wadi ≥30l/m² of disconnected roof), each up to €5,000 per activity (and never more than actual costs incurred, per invoices/proof of payment). Excludes: measures already carried out before the (complete) application is submitted; work required by law/regulation; replacement of similar existing measures; use of leaching materials (copper, zinc, lead, nickel, chromium); measures for which subsidy was already received for the same roof/part under this scheme; applications from national/provincial/municipal/water-authority bodies; and costs already funded/applied for via another subsidy scheme for similar activities. [Separately, under a distinct Oss municipal scheme, wood-stove removal and flue decommissioning is covered up to €1,000 -- this is a different subsidy, not part of the climate-adaptation cost-coverage scope.]

Covers: per-measure fixed amounts / per-unit or per-m² rates / percentage-of-quote amounts for a specified list of sustainability measures (solar boiler, heat pump boiler, shower heat exchanger, home battery, roof/floor/ground/cavity/panel/solid-wall insulation, HR++/HR+++ glazing, green roof covering, induction cooktop with gas disconnection, heat network connection for social organisations, rain barrel, rainwater tank/water storage bag, LED sports-field lighting, asbestos roof removal), each capped at its own unit rate/%, all within an overall €2,500/dwelling ceiling (higher separate ceilings apply for some measures e.g. heat network €5,000, LED lighting €2,500). Excludes: solar panels (no subsidy, only a loan), costs beyond the quoted/norm price, VAT/administrative costs, maintenance and monitoring costs, and general permitting costs (except a partial discount on permit fees when cavity-wall/roof structural change requires one); businesses/companies (bedrijven) and other institutions (other than "maatschappelijke organisaties" for their buildings) are excluded from applying at all; tenants cannot apply directly.

Covers a percentage of eligible material and installation/labour costs for each specific green/water measure under the 'Stimuleringsregeling Roosendaal Natuurstad' umbrella: for green roofs, 35% of costs (substrate <40mm) or 45% (substrate ≥40mm), subject to minimum specifications (≥25 L/m² retention, ≥8 plant species) and maximum caps (€3,000 for private individuals; €6,000 for VvE/businesses); other sub-measures (façade gardens, tree planting, rain barrels/water storage, rainwater disconnection, permeable paving, depaving/'tegel eruit groen erin') are covered under the same scheme but their specific percentage/cap details are not stated in the sources reviewed. Excludes: costs for structural adaptations to roof constructions or canopies (dakconstructies of overkappingen) for the green roof measure; design, permitting, maintenance and monitoring costs are not mentioned as covered.

Covers: green roofs, green façades, garden greening (native and non-native planting, with bonus for native 'Plantenlijst' species), tree planting (bonus for native trees), rainwater storage/rain barrels/cisterns (min. 500L storage from min. 3m² connected paved surface), connection of rainwater downspouts to separated sewer systems, and heat-mitigation measures. Excludes: not stated whether design/permitting/monitoring/ongoing maintenance costs are covered; non-native, non-listed plantings receive only the base €10/m² rate without species bonus.

Covers: realisation/installation costs of eligible green-blue measures -- depaving/greening (per m² of tiles removed), permeable paving, green/blue (sedum) roof or infiltration facility, downspout disconnection (rain-pipe decoupling), rain barrel purchase, and green façade (min. 2m²) -- reimbursed via per-measure caps (e.g. up to €2,500 for depaving or green façade, up to €10,000 for green/blue roof or infiltration facility, €50 per address for downspout disconnection and rain barrel), with the total grant capped at max 30% of actually incurred/documented costs (invoices and bank statements required at completion), except the rain barrel/downspout €50 flat amounts which are excluded from the 30%-of-actual-costs cap. Excludes: costs for a measure already previously subsidised at the same address/for the same measure, work started before approval, and (implicitly) maintenance or design-only costs since only "realisation" (aanleg/uitvoering) costs are compensated; activities must be completed within 6 months of approval or the grant decision is withdrawn.

Direct and necessary water-storage costs remaining after third-party contributions; 100% for Ooievaarspas holders or 50% otherwise, capped at €500/1,000 litres and applicable programme maxima. Excludes duplicate funding, structural works (constructieve voorzieningen), replacement of existing planting and water-permeable surfaces, recoverable VAT and applicant labour (eigen inzet).

Covers a percentage or fixed per-m² share of actual invoiced installation/construction costs (evidenced by quote at application, invoice at settlement) for six measures: green roof, green façade, depaving (to green or semi-permeable surface), water storage/wadi, infiltration systems, and rainwater downspout disconnection -- per the rate table (e.g. green roof/façade 50% up to €25-40/m²; depaving €5-10/m²; wadi/infiltration/downspout disconnection 60% of costs). Excludes: costs not evidenced by invoice/quote; self-performed (DIY) labour costs (only materials count when work is done by the applicant, per worked example); work/costs incurred before the application is submitted (works must not have started); areas below the 6 m² minimum for green roof/façade or depaving; and a second subsidy for the same measure on the same cadastral parcel. Maintenance, design/planning and monitoring costs are not mentioned as covered .

Covers: garden/façade greening materials and installation (tiles removal, façade-garden packages, tree pits, rain barrels at discount, green/blue roofs), plus separate KIEM grants for community nature/greening projects (plants, seeds, tools, educational materials, volunteer-based projects). Excludes: KIEM specifically excludes paving/paths, water piping systems, greenhouses, storage sheds, walls, bike sheds, seating/benches, picnic tables, and indirect purchases like vehicles, computers, toilets; guidance/supervision costs capped at 30% of total KIEM project costs.

Covers: realized/incurred material and labour costs ("gemaakte kosten") for eligible measures -- downspout disconnection (regenpijp doorzagen/vrij laten afstromen), underground infiltration, connection to municipal rainwater sewer, garden greening/depaving ("ontstenen en vergroenen"), green roof installation, façade greenery and façade-garden planting -- each reimbursed at fixed per-m²/per-unit rates (e.g. €10/m² for disconnection measures, €10/m² for greening, €30/m² for green roof, €15 per plant for façade greenery, €20 per façade garden), up to per-parcel maxima (€350 for disconnection alone [note: capped table elsewhere states €2,000/parcel for disconnection], €2,000 combined for depaving/greening); for organisations, a flat €2,000 covering the same measures or an educational activity. Excludes: costs exceeding the per-m²/unit rates or the per-parcel/flat maximum; no coverage stated for design/planning, permitting, ongoing maintenance, or monitoring costs (applicants must submit design drawings and quotes as part of the application, but these preparatory costs are not listed as reimbursable).

Covers: costs of disconnecting rainwater from roofs and paved surfaces (e.g. terrace, driveway, garage) from the combined/foul sewer on private land (min. 10 m² up to 300 m² at a flat €11/m²; above 300 m² reimbursed at actual construction cost up to a €11/m² cap), including construction of the required on-site storage/infiltration facility (min. 20mm available storage capacity, processed within 48 hours), plus a free, non-binding advisory site visit. Excludes: a standalone rain barrel not connected to a storage/infiltration facility; disconnected area below 10 m²; surfaces for which subsidy was previously requested/granted; disconnection causing nuisance to surroundings; and ongoing maintenance/repair costs and damage from improper installation or insufficient upkeep, which remain the owner's responsibility.

Covers on-site private measures to reduce stormwater runoff/drought impact: replacing paved surface with permeable surfaces, constructing rainwater storage/reuse (waterberging), and disconnecting paved roof surfaces from the combined sewer system; available to homeowners, tenants, owners' associations (VvE) and non-profit organisations. Excludes schools, housing corporations, and for-profit organisations from eligibility (specific covered cost types beyond installation, e.g. design/maintenance fees, not stated).
Green-roof materials and installation only

Covers: one-third of total green roof installation project costs (labour/materials/quantities per quote), up to €3,000/year/applicant; separate €250/yr for structural/building advice on roof suitability. Excludes: annual/ongoing maintenance of the green roof, tools for installation, roofs installed before 1 July 2024, and any roof already receiving another government financial contribution/subsidy for green roof installation.
Covers reasonable costs directly connected to implementing eligible measures; excludes application-preparation costs and costs connected with obtaining required permits
Tangible goods for biodiversity work, including plants, trapping equipment and herbicide; applicant contribution may include labour and vehicle expenses

Covers: reduced/discounted municipal building-permit case-processing fee (gebyr) for establishing green roofs/façades and for solar-integrated roof/façade material; free fee for the initial digital eligibility inquiry (whether a permit is needed) when the measure only concerns green roof/façade. Not covered/excluded: costs of design, construction, planting materials, installation labour, or maintenance are not addressed as covered items in the provided sources; additional fees still apply for dispensations, work started before permit, or other measures bundled into the same application

Covers documented costs of purchasing/installing a rainwater retention tank (underground, above-ground, allotment-garden above-ground) or converting an existing septic tank/household sewage plant into a sealed rainwater retention tank, up to fixed caps per type; excludes other stormwater/green infrastructure measures (no green roofs, façades, rain gardens, permeable paving, or trees)

Covers 100% of documented/eligible construction costs of a residential rain garden, up to a cap of 4,000 zł (individuals, legal entities, entrepreneurs) or 10,000 zł (housing communities/cooperatives); excludes costs above the cap and any costs incurred before application approval/before works start; funding requires post-completion verification (signed completion protocol with photo documentation) and is conditioned on (repayable if breached) a ≥3-year maintenance obligation borne by the applicant, with no ongoing maintenance funding; applicant must hold ownership/legal title to property within Gdańsk city limits.
80% of eligible costs, maximum PLN 10,000; covers design, geological studies, purchase, transport, installation and limited earthworks; only costs after contract signature

Covers: purchase, assembly/installation, construction and commissioning of rainwater harvesting infrastructure -- surface freestanding sealed tanks and underground sealed tanks (tiered by capacity), plus conveyance pipework (gutters/inlets to tank). Excludes: costs already incurred/investments completed before application submission; only one grant permitted per property (ever); does not mention coverage of design/planning, permitting, maintenance or monitoring costs.

Covers: purchase and installation ("necessary") costs of the qualifying rainwater micro-retention measures -- underground/above-ground rainwater tanks, bioretention systems, drainage systems, irrigation systems for green/wooded areas and gardens, and extensive/intensive green roofs -- plus costs of modernising an existing installation to enable its connection to one of these systems; funding is capped at 80% of necessary gross costs incurred, subject to per-measure ceilings (e.g. PLN 12,000 caps, unit rates per m³/m²/mb). Excludes: costs/expenses incurred outside the task's implementation period stated in the grant contract; tasks on properties that already have the same type of system installed; equipment/installations not permanently affixed to the property (i.e. not guaranteeing a durable ecological effect, such as those on unfenced plots vulnerable to damage); and double-financing of the same costs from other non-repayable sources.
Rainwater and stormwater retention and management works only

Covers: materials, installation/construction of new stormwater retention systems (tanks/cisterns, submersible pumps, connection elements), wall greening (climbing plants on facades ≥10m²), rain gardens, and materials/works for modernising/upgrading existing rainwater systems. Excludes: costs unrelated to these three measure types; property must have settled legal status and applicant must hold legal title to it.

Covers (2025 municipal small-retention grant): purchase and installation/mounting ("montaż") of new retention devices -- underground and above-ground rainwater tanks, pumps, discharge outlets, and gutter-fed rain barrels; funding is capped at 80% of necessary costs (max 5,000 PLN/property for individuals, 10,000 PLN for others), and costs are only recognised if incurred after signing the agreement with the municipality (costs before the agreement are excluded). Design/planning fees, permitting fees, and ongoing maintenance/monitoring costs are not mentioned as eligible. Not applicable / separate scheme: the city page also references the distinct, earlier "Moja Woda" regional programme (WFOŚiGW Warszawa, applications closed 30.06.2024), which additionally covered purchase/delivery/installation/construction/commissioning of rainwater collection, ground-infiltration, and green-roof drainage-layer (excluding planting costs) equipment, with eligible costs restricted to 01.01.2023-30.06.2024 -- this is a separate funding stream, not part of the current 2025 municipal grant's cost-coverage scope.

Covers (eligible costs, per measure): (1) Retention tanks (above/underground): purchase, assembly, construction and commissioning of installations enabling management of rain/meltwater on the property, incl. discharge pipes/conduits, tanks, pumps. (2) Rain garden: cost of materials needed to build the rain garden plus hydrophilic plants. Excludes: any costs incurred before the grant agreement is signed; design/permitting, monitoring and ongoing maintenance costs are not listed as eligible . Structural conditions bounding eligibility: only non-business-use residential parcels with no outstanding dues to the city may apply, and only one grant per property parcel per 5 years.
Up to 80%/PLN 1,500 for purchase and installation of above-ground tanks (minimum 500 L total), underground tanks (minimum 2,000 L), ponds (minimum 500 L), or rain gardens

Covers: installation costs of on-site rainwater/meltwater retention devices (container rain garden, in-ground rain garden, infiltration well, above-ground free-standing rainwater tank fed from roof, underground rainwater tank). Excludes: already-completed investments (applications must be submitted before works start). Detailed rules on what costs qualify/are excluded (design, permitting, maintenance, documentation) are said to be in a separate linked document ("Szczegółowe informacje... TUTAJ") and are Not stated on this page.

Covers 80% of eligible/incurred costs ("poniesionych kosztów kwalifikowanych") for constructing: (1) above-ground closed freestanding rainwater storage tanks with gutter connection installation, (2) underground rainwater storage tanks, (3) bioretention systems using rainwater (min. 100m² for individuals, 500m² for HOAs/legal entities/businesses), and (4) irrigation systems for green areas using rainwater (same area thresholds); per-measure grant amounts are capped by tank capacity/system type tiers as listed. Excludes: systems below the minimum area thresholds; costs not incurred for the defined tasks. Not stated: coverage of design/planning, permitting, maintenance, or monitoring costs.
Devices, materials and construction works associated with qualifying retention installations

Covers up to 80% of actual/documented investment realisation costs (installed equipment/urządzenia, built-in materials, and works/installation) for the two eligible categories only-retention-infiltration devices (urządzenia retencyjno-rozsączające) and sealed retention tanks (zbiorniki retencyjne)-subject to caps (4,000 zł individuals/sole traders; 10,000 zł other non-public-finance-sector entities; up to 80% uncapped for public-finance-sector municipal/county legal persons); excludes costs incurred before the grant agreement is signed, and implicitly excludes devices/measures outside these two categories

Up to 80% of documented implementation costs for eligible retention/infiltration devices and storage reservoirs; applicant must submit invoices, evidence of completed work and photographs; maintenance and design costs not stated

Covers: purchase and installation of rainwater-harvesting/retention devices (above- and underground tanks, infiltration wells/swales ("studnie chłonne"), green/retention roofs, rain gardens), plus associated earthworks and surface reinstatement after works -- funded up to 80% of costs, capped at 5,000 zł (up to 8,000 zł for larger underground tanks) for individuals and 10,000 zł for communities/cooperatives. Excludes (not stated as covered): costs beyond the 80%/cap limits, and design/planning, permitting, ongoing maintenance, and monitoring costs .

Covers: provision (loan then transfer of ownership) of one rainwater/stormwater collection tank (zbiornik na wody opadowe i roztopowe) per eligible property. Excludes/not stated: installation labour, design/planning, permitting, ongoing maintenance, and monitoring costs.

Covered: installation costs, green roof/vertical greenery systems, root barriers, waterproofing, supporting structures, plant materials, plant media, irrigation, drainage materials, consultancy/PE fees, authority submissions. Excluded: maintenance, lighting, artificial plants, hardscape, signages, GST, movable pots

Covers up to 50% of actual/invested (post-implementation, incurred) costs of implementing eligible rainwater management measures -- e.g. drainage/seepage systems and rain gardens, rainwater collection/storage/filtering equipment and pumps, permeable paving, green roofs/green walls, and household reuse systems (materials/equipment purchase and construction works) -- reimbursed only after project completion, capped at €1,000 per applicant; excludes design/planning, permitting, maintenance and monitoring costs (not mentioned as covered)

Covers eligible project implementation costs (up to 70% of approved eligible costs, paid in two tranches: 70% after contract signing, 30% after final accounting) for public-benefit, non-commercial activities carried out within the target calendar year (2025: 01.01-15.12.2025; 2026: 01.01-15.12.2026) in one of the funded thematic areas (incl. environment/public space priority actions such as rain gardens, permeable surfaces, green roofs, invasive-species control, etc.); requires minimum 30% applicant co-financing, of which unpaid volunteer labour may cover up to 15% (2025 call) / 50% (2026 call); excludes commercial-character projects, organizations founded/funded by the city itself, and political parties/movements; does not cover costs outside the project period or long-term post-project maintenance/monitoring as a distinct funded item

Covers (§11, pressupost subvencionable): construction/works costs; non-recoverable/non-compensable VAT; general expenses; industrial profit imputable to the works; technical fees (honoraris tècnics) tied to the action; complementary technical reports (e.g. chromatic, historic studies); taxes/fees derived from the building permit; and other duly justified expenses derived from the action. Excludes (§6, immovable-property eligibility requirements, which condition what actuations/costs can be funded at all): whole-building use changes; demolition retaining only façades; real-estate promotion works; largely vacant buildings (<70% permanent occupancy in the prior two years); buildings with horizontal-division/segregation of >40% of units in the prior two years; and premises with a change of use/activity/ownership in the prior two years (except ownership changes among co-owners within a community of property). Also structurally excluded/non-covered: any expedient below the €1,000 minimum expenditure threshold (§10.1.a), and post-completion/ongoing maintenance is not listed among eligible cost categories in §11 (only the 5-year maintenance-of-conditions obligation is imposed, not funded).
Works, equipment, auxiliary installations, permits, reports, certificates and technical studies; IVA where non-recoverable

Covers: green roofs and green façades on buildings, tree care/pruning of protected private trees, biodiversity/climate-adaptation greening measures (green spaces, meadows, hedges, ponds) via the value-capture (Mehrwertabgabefonds) fund, and combined green-roof+PV installations. Excludes/unclear: no confirmed coverage of rain barrels/cisterns, no stated coverage of new tree planting itself (only care of existing protected trees), ongoing maintenance/upkeep costs explicitly remain owner's responsibility (façade greening), and specific eligible cost sub-types (design, permitting, monitoring) are not detailed in provided sources.

Covers: cost of supply and installation ("fourniture et pose") of rainwater-reuse equipment (tanks/cisterns plastic or concrete, filters, mobile/fixed pumps, overflow connection to drainage network), for outdoor/garden watering (or other stated non-domestic use), limited to the actual installation cost and to CHF 500/owner max (graduated CHF 1/litre for 150-500L). Excludes: installations whose water ends up in wastewater/domestic (indoor) use; and, for construction/renovation projects already legally required under RETE to have stormwater management measures, only the additional volume dedicated to reuse beyond the mandatory volume is subsidy-eligible (i.e., the RETE-mandated volume itself is excluded).

Covers up to 50% of project costs for private individuals/businesses undertaking rainwater retention, infiltration, or on-site reuse measures -- e.g. desealing (Entsiegelung), greening/green roofs and façades, creation/preservation of green and unsealed areas, climate-adapted building/infrastructure design, and promotion of water surfaces. Excludes (not documented as covered): the remaining share of project costs (fund covers only up to half), and standard drinking-water/wastewater infrastructure, which is run separately by municipal utilities (Entsorgung St.Gallen / St.Galler Stadtwerke) and is not part of the fund's scope.

Covers: green roofs (extensive/intensive) incl. establishment maintenance; vertical/façade greening incl. establishment maintenance; ecological upgrading of outdoor spaces; desealing/depaving of sealed surfaces; tree planting incl. development-phase maintenance; preservation/care of valuable existing trees. Grant = 50% of total costs per final invoice, capped at CHF 1,000,000 per measure. Excludes/not mentioned: rain gardens, bioswales, permeable paving as distinct category, rain barrels/cisterns, and ongoing (post-establishment) long-term maintenance beyond the initial creation/establishment period.
Approved renovation materials and construction/installation costs only; all other costs are expressly excluded

Covers project delivery/installation costs for community greening and biodiversity projects on publicly accessible sites within Westminster, completed within one year of grant award, where environmental impact/carbon footprint/climate resilience and biodiversity measures have been considered; excludes ongoing maintenance costs (grant funding cannot be used for maintenance), though applicants must plan for future management/maintenance for at least 5 years post-completion as an eligibility condition; Professionals category applicants must additionally provide ≥25% match funding.

Covers: lawn removal/conversion labor or self-installation reimbursed per sq.ft. (standard/super/median strip rates), tree installation (Treebate), 2-hour landscape design consultation (LDAP). Excludes: artificial turf, non-permeable hardscape, non-biodegradable weed barriers, moderate/high-water or invasive plants, keeping existing sprinklers/adjustable emitters, projects already started before approval, ongoing maintenance costs, permitting fees, monitoring costs.

Covers: subsidised rain barrel unit (55-gallon), flexible connecting elbow, linking hose to a second barrel, leaf/mosquito filter screen, spigot, overflow hose, detailed instructions, and free delivery. Excludes: professional installation labor, ongoing maintenance costs, and any liability for malfunction/damage (explicitly disclaimed).
Covers qualifying rain barrels/cisterns designed for rain capture; 50-gallon minimum per barrel. Installation costs not stated as eligible.

Covers partial purchase cost (up to stated per-unit/per-household caps) of qualifying water-saving devices under the SGVMWD rebate program: water flow monitors, rain barrels/cisterns, water-efficient washing machines, weather-based irrigation controllers, soil moisture sensor systems, high-efficiency toilets, commercial waterless urinals, and rotating sprinkler nozzles. Excludes (not mentioned/covered): design or planning costs, permitting, installation labor, and ongoing maintenance/monitoring costs .

Direct-install turf replacement covering assessment, 50% of design, per-square-foot turf incentive, and part of labour/material/installation costs; customer pays remaining project costs and maintains the landscape for five years

Rebate calculated by eligible converted turf area; project must include drought-tolerant planting, irrigation modification and stormwater retention/filtration; synthetic turf is excluded; separate device rebates may also apply

Covers materials and contracted labour for approved BMP installation; 50% reimbursement up to US$1,800 combined, or US$75 for a rain barrel; prior approval required; completed receipts/invoices required. Other exclusions not stated.

Provides recurring quarterly stormwater-bill credits for qualifying rain barrels, rain gardens, cisterns, dry wells, RiverSafe participation and compliant stormwater controls. It does not reimburse purchase or installation costs .

Covers: cost of lawn removal and replacement with water-wise plants (up to $1/sq ft, capped by site type), plus optional discounted add-ons (design consultation up to $200, drip irrigation design assistance, plant/mulch discount coupons). Excludes: costs of hardscape beyond the 20% non-permeable allowance, ongoing irrigation/water bills, and any project work done before CCWD's Notice to Proceed approval (non-retroactive)
Utility-fee reduction rather than cost reimbursement; no installation, design or maintenance expenditure is expressly reimbursed
Pays per qualifying turf area converted; impervious surfaces, structures, synthetic turf and nonqualifying plant areas are excluded
Covers workshop materials for constructing one take-home rain barrel and practical instruction. Installation labour and maintenance support are not stated.

Covers: provision of one free rain barrel per attendee at bi-annual workshops, plus optional second barrel and DIY kit purchase for $30; DIY build instructions/kit information available on request. Excludes: rain gardens, green roofs, permeable paving, trees, and any direct cash grants or ongoing maintenance costs -- not covered or not mentioned.
Incentive is based on approved turf-conversion area; nonapproved areas, structures, artificial turf and impervious surfaces are excluded

Covers (rebates/grants -- purchase and installation costs, and some free items/services): landscape conversion (turf-to-native/WaterWise Landscape), landscape survival tools (mulch/compost/aeration), WaterWise Rainscape features, rainwater harvesting systems (rain barrels/cisterns), irrigation upgrades, pressure regulating valves, watering timers, laundry-to-landscape graywater systems, pool filter and pool cover equipment; free residential conservation tools (showerheads, aerators, soil moisture meters, hose meters, sunlight calculators, mulch pickup) and free irrigation system evaluations; grant funding (up to 75% of cost, capped) for water efficiency audits; grants for urban forest projects, Bright Green Futures school sustainability projects, and Community Outreach/Neighborhood Partnering community grants. Excludes/not stated: ongoing or annual maintenance costs, permitting fees, monitoring costs, green roofs/green façades, permeable paving, and general tree planting are not mentioned as covered.

Covers qualifying purchases for xeriscape conversion, rainwater collection systems, low-flow fixtures, smart irrigation controllers and high-efficiency washers, subject to component-specific requirements and caps; the current page does not establish labour, design, permitting, maintenance or monitoring cost coverage

Covers: a credit/reduction against the recurring Stormwater (Remediation) Fee bill line item for property owners (single-family and non-single-family) who install and maintain qualifying stormwater treatment practices (e.g., trees, rain gardens, rain barrels, and other BMPs per the Guidance Documents) and/or accumulate volunteer clean-up hours; also covers small-lot impervious-area exemptions, NPDES industrial discharge permit holder credit, private storm drain owner credit, privately-maintained public cemetery street credit, faith-organization place-of-worship/school fee reductions, and hardship exemptions for eligible tax-exempt organizations via an alternative compliance plan. Excludes: no direct cash grant, reimbursement, or subsidy for upfront capital/installation costs, and no documented coverage of design, permitting, or monitoring costs -- relief is limited to reducing/exempting the ongoing fee itself, not funding the practices.

Covers: subsidised purchase price of rain barrel/composter units picked up at a City DPW event. Excludes: installation labor, design/permitting, maintenance, and monitoring costs -- none mentioned in sources.
Per-square-foot contribution toward qualifying turf conversion; commercial payment cannot exceed eligible programme costs and excludes applicant labour, tools and off-area materials

Covers: lawn removal (physical removal or sheet mulching), low-water-use/CA native plant material covering ≥50% of converted area, mulch (min. 3in) or compost (super rebate), irrigation conversion (sprinkler removal/capping or drip conversion with pressure regulator/filter), permeable hardscape elements set in sand/gravel/DG, and optionally a tree (via linked Treebate) and design consultation (via LDAP), all calculated per sq.ft. of converted lawn area up to property caps ($2,000 residential/$15,000 commercial per 24 months). Excludes: artificial turf/turf alternatives, non-permeable hardscape (concrete, mortar-set pavers), non-biodegradable weed barriers, rock/mulch-only areas without plants, moderate-to-high water use or invasive plants, and any project work started before EBMUD approval (not retroactive).

Discounted purchase covers a 55-gallon rain-barrel unit, instructions, leaf/mosquito screen, downspout connector, spigot, overflow hose, tax and delivery; the resident self-installs and the dossier does not establish programme coverage of labour or maintenance materials

Covers installation costs of eligible RainScapes stormwater-management practices (rain gardens, conservation landscapes, green roofs, permeable pavers, pavement removal, rain barrels/cisterns/water harvesting) on residential, commercial, institutional, HOA, and nonprofit properties, up to per-property rebate caps ($7,500 residential; $20,000 commercial/institutional/HOA/nonprofit); does not state coverage of design/planning, permitting, maintenance, or monitoring costs

Covers: a percentage credit (up to 50%) against the City's stormwater collection and management user fee for non-residential properties and low-income residential parcels, subject to application via Credit Application Form or Structure Certification Form and possible appeal. Excludes/Not stated: no direct capital grants, loans, rebates outside the fee-credit mechanism, and no specific list of eligible BMP types or cost categories could be confirmed from the extractable text (Credit and Appeals Manual PDF was image-based/non-machine-readable).

Grant (current, 2025 version): BWSC pays 100% of eligible project costs, capped at $8,000 per property per 10 years (Education Grant exempt from the 10-year limit), broken down by category -- Water Quality (SRP customers only): 100% of eligible materials costs (no mention of labor coverage in current version) for infiltration infrastructure (cisterns/French drains ≥200 gal, rain gardens ≥100 sq ft), native tree plantings, and native vegetation plantings; Habitat Restoration: reimburses 100% of materials costs (not contracted labor) for practices like vegetation management, invasive plant control, stream/wetland restoration, stream buffers, revegetation; Environmental Education: 100% of eligible project costs (e.g., transportation, materials) but explicitly excludes labor costs. Excluded across all categories: projects/practices already required by regulation; practices already constructed or completed before approval; Water Quality practices required as part of the new development/site-plan process; costs above the $8,000 cap; permitting costs (applicant must separately obtain required local/state/federal permits) and ongoing maintenance are not listed as covered. Covers: turf/lawn removal (via Resource Central's Removal Service at a discounted rate, or DIY removal), waterwise/native perennial garden installation (up to four free Garden-in-a-Box kits for DIY option, or discount for professional removal), landscape conversion cost discount up to $750 (while supplies last, HB-1151 funded), and free/no-cost irrigation audits ("Slow the Flow"), free waterwise yard seminars, and free technical/educational resources (demonstration gardens). One recycled rain barrel per eligible household; additional barrels purchased separately; other costs not stated

Covers: lawn-to-drought-tolerant-landscape conversion, drip-irrigation conversion, pool covers, high-efficiency toilets and clothes washers, commercial irrigation-only meters, and commercial potable-to-non-potable conversion, subject to the stated caps

Covers: reduced purchase price of a rain barrel and/or compost bin (including kitchen collector pail) ordered via RAM, with optional free local pickup. Qualifying turf conversion, planting, permeable landscaping, irrigation modification and stormwater-retention features within the approved project area
