Covers material/installation costs of qualifying LCW landscaping projects (rain garden, native garden, shoreline restoration) up to a $250 Lakeville city utility bill rebate (not exceeding total project cost); excludes owner's personal labor/time, costs already reimbursed by an LCW grant, and work within public right-of-way/easements; related but distinct county/state programs (Dakota County SWCD LCW Grant up to $400; Lawns to Legumes up to $350 after 25% cost match) cover overlapping but separately-administered project costs

Covers turf-removal projects, subsurface irrigation, and purchase/installation of specified water-saving devices. Explicit exclusions include synthetic turf, nonporous concrete/tile, driveway-extension projects and projects started before pre-approval. Other cost categories Not stated.

Covers: cash rebate per sq ft for grass removal and desert-landscape installation (plants, irrigation, hardscape elements up to the qualifying area), plus $100/tree bonus. Excludes: design/planning fees, permit costs, and removal costs for existing landscape elements not part of the new design (borne by applicant); non-permeable hardscape (concrete patios, driveways, curbing) excluded from conversion area calculation; maintenance costs not covered.

Covers: subsidised purchase price of the rain barrel unit itself ($78 vs $154 retail) and a $25/barrel utility bill credit for up to 2 installations per household per year. Excludes: commercial water customers (residential only), design/permitting/monitoring costs, ongoing maintenance costs, and any barrels beyond the 2-per-household cap or beyond the 200-customer rebate quota.

Covers 75% of eligible materials and/or contractor labour for approved rain gardens, native plantings, native trees, cisterns, permeable pavers and rain barrels; total cap US$1,500, with listed unit caps. Some ornamentals, hardscaping and edging may be excluded or prorated. Mandatory development projects are ineligible.

Covers (as bill credits, not upfront rebates): purchase cost of qualifying low-flow toilet (up to $50; residence built pre-2005 only, must be WaterSense certified), high-efficiency washing machine (up to $75), rain barrel (up to $25), and a mandatory irrigation system inspection performed by a city-registered/licensed irrigation professional (up to $50) -- all capped at a combined $375 per single-family residential address per fiscal year. Excludes: installation/labor costs beyond the purchase price, design/planning, permitting, ongoing maintenance and monitoring costs, and any non-listed water-conserving improvements (e.g., green infrastructure such as green roofs, rain gardens, permeable paving, trees). Requires original invoice/sales receipt and proof-of-purchase barcode; limited to single-family residential utility customers.

Covers up to 80% of total project cost for feasibility/design studies and design-and-construction/installation of qualifying stormwater quality projects (e.g., rain gardens, bioretention, rainwater harvesting, pervious pavement, stream restoration/cleaning, constructed wetlands, tree planting/canopy, storm drain marking, retention pond enhancement, rain barrel installation, education seminars/brochures), subject to maximum grant caps that vary by class and project type (Class A Neighborhood: $45,000 feasibility / $120,000 award; Class B Infrastructure: $55,000 feasibility / $360,000 design-and-construction); excludes the remaining 20% cost share, which the applicant must fund via cash or in-kind donation, and ongoing/routine post-completion maintenance costs, which are not stated as covered .

Covers 50% of qualifying expenses for approved rain gardens/bioswales, waterwise lawns and pavement removal, plus eligible add-ons, capped at US$2,000. Work cannot begin before approval. Project-specific reimbursable/non-reimbursable lists determine detailed coverage.

Covers: subsidised rain barrel unit (55-gallon capacity), flexible downspout connecting elbow, linking hose for connecting a second barrel, leaf/mosquito filter screen, spigot/tap, overflow hose, and free delivery. Excludes: installation labor/tools (hacksaw, platform materials, garden hose beyond what's included, concrete blocks/wood for stand -- user-supplied), any repair/replacement beyond manufacturer warranty, and ongoing maintenance costs.

Covers: purchase cost of qualified drought-tolerant plants, mulch, compost, permeable hardscape materials, and drip irrigation supplies used in the lawn-to-garden conversion. Excludes: sales tax, deliveries, installation, labor, personal items, equipment rental, tools, artificial turf, non-biodegradable weed block materials, and non-permeable hardscapes.

Covered: landscape/irrigation conversion and equipment rebates -- turf replacement, Native Plant Parkway conversion, Direct Install Gardens, and Lawn to Garden (all via LB Utilities), plus equipment rebates (smart controllers, rain barrels, irrigation nozzles) via SoCal WaterSmart; tree planting outside homes via Tree Planting Program; mulch via Mulch Pick Up & Delivery Program. MWELO itself is a regulatory design/installation/maintenance compliance framework for qualifying new (≥500 sq ft) and rehabilitated (≥2500 sq ft) landscapes and is not itself a cost-covering/funding mechanism, though it cross-references the LB Utilities and SoCal WaterSmart rebate programs. Not covered/not stated: green roofs, green façades, rain gardens/bioswales, permeable paving, and ongoing landscape maintenance costs; no dollar caps or disbursement details are stated in these sources.

Qualifying landscape scope includes turf removal and conversion incorporating plants, groundcover and a required/qualifying rain-capture feature; precise reimbursable cost categories and exclusions are Not stated.

Covers: purchase, installation, and connection costs of up to two newly purchased, approved rain barrels per customer account/master meter (min. 40 gal each), reimbursed at 85% of cost up to $400 per barrel, not to exceed actual cost. Excludes: sales tax, accessories, delivery/shipping, extra materials, and labor/installation costs beyond the rebate cap; homemade rain barrels; pre-owned or leased barrels; barrels connected to an irrigation system or requiring pumps/backflow devices; and new construction.
Covers part of the rain-barrel purchase price; barrel includes spigot, plugs, screen, lid, overflow valves and flex tube; diverter and polished stones are additional

Covers: hard costs (materials and installation of the green roof system) and soft costs (design, site investigations, management), up to the maximum reimbursement value calculated via the GRA × soil-depth reimbursement schedule (with a $50,000 project minimum), and with soft costs capped at 20% of hard costs. Excludes: costs not related to the design and construction of the green roof; costs to meet regulatory requirements the property is already subject to; and the solar portion of a combined green/solar roof system (matching funds required for that portion).

Covers the discounted purchase price of the Ivy rain barrel unit (subsidised to $78.00 from $162.99 retail), including its built-in overflow hose and debris/mosquito-guard screening; excludes installation labor, design/planning, permitting, maintenance, and monitoring costs -- none of which are mentioned in the source
Provides access to a discounted barrel and central pickup ; installation and accessory coverage not stated
Covers: purchase of one new ≥40-gallon rain barrel. Excludes: tax, installation, accessories and other related items.

Grass removal and replacement with qualifying low-water-use landscape achieving at least 50% mature plant canopy coverage in the converted area; optional one-two-tree bonus; artificial turf or rock alone excluded

Covers: cost of the rain barrel purchase itself (HDPE, ≥50 gal, spigot+gasket), up to $50 or purchase price whichever is less. Excludes: installation costs, other related items, permitting/contractor costs (explicitly noted installation may require a permit/licensed contractor at owner's expense), and ongoing maintenance (owner responsibility, e.g., annual cleaning).

Covers qualifying barrel purchase price and required components, excluding sales tax, installation, permits, contractor costs, and other related items; purchase price or USD 50 maximum per barrel; two rebates per property lifetime

Covers: discounted purchase price of a rain barrel or compost bin plus instructional guidance (diverter setup, care/use). Excludes: installation labor beyond basic diverter setup, ongoing maintenance costs, design/permitting, and monitoring.

Covers: subsidized purchase price of the 50-gallon Ivy rain barrel kit (barrel plus assembly hardware -- 6' overflow hose, screen/screen ring, ball valve, ziplock ties, overflow cap) for verified Millcreek residents, limited to 2 subsidized barrels per household (additional barrels available at full $88 price). Excludes: professional installation labor, design/planning, permitting, and ongoing maintenance/monitoring costs -- residents self-install using included instructions/videos.
Rain barrels: equipment and downspout-diversion kit only; cisterns: eligible storage capacity; rain gardens: contributing roof area; labour, installation, delivery, hauling and tax excluded

Covers: monthly stormwater utility fee reduction (35% flat, 45% in Green Zones) for approved BMPs (rain garden, pervious pavement, green roof, stormwater reuse) installed and maintained on the applicant's own private property, treating runoff from impervious areas on that property. Excludes: rain barrels (explicitly ineligible), any practices installed in the public right-of-way, and no direct capital grant or reimbursement for installation costs is provided -- only the recurring fee discount.
Covers purchase of qualifying manufactured barrels/cisterns; homemade systems are excluded; barrel minimum 50 gallons; cistern minimum 200 gallons; receipt and water bill required
Qualifying turf conversion with plants, stormwater-retention feature and other programme requirements; separate device rebates may include rain barrels/cisterns

Covers: purchase price of rain barrel unit (55-gallon), leaf/mosquito filter screen, spigot, flexible downspout connecting elbow, overflow hose, and free delivery to home. Excludes: installation labor, tools (hacksaw, platform materials), maintenance/winterization costs, and any damage/liability from use.

Rain barrels: equipment and downspout-diversion kit only; cisterns: eligible storage capacity; rain gardens: contributing roof area. Rain-barrel labour, installation, delivery, hauling and tax are excluded.

Covers the purchase/rebate cost of qualifying water-efficiency and landscaping devices (premium high-efficiency toilets, urinals, high-efficiency clothes washers, PRVs, leak detectors/monitors, rain barrels, cisterns, rotating sprinkler nozzles, weather-based irrigation controllers, soil moisture sensors, turf replacement) plus select non-device items (leak repair bill credit, car wash rebate, Living Coast Discovery Center admission credit); excludes design/planning, permitting, installation labor/plumbing modification costs, ongoing maintenance and monitoring service costs; does not cover green roofs, green façades, rain gardens/bioswales, permeable paving, or tree planting as these categories are not listed on the programme page

Covers: cost of the rain barrel unit itself (subsidised), connecting elbow, linking hose, delivery/shipping. Excludes: installation labor/tools (hacksaw, platform materials, garden hose for overflow -- resident's responsibility), ongoing maintenance/winterization labor, and any malfunction/damage liability

Covers purchase/installation (capital) costs of qualifying rebate measures -- drought-tolerant tree purchase/planting, Comal County Gardening Guide purchase, AC/heat pump/window unit/mini-split replacement, ENERGY STAR/CEE ultra-high efficiency washing machine, programmable/smart thermostats, annual AC/heat pump checkup/servicing, turfgrass removal, soil amendments (mulch/compost/aeration), irrigation zone removal, rain barrels/cisterns, and residential/commercial solar panel installation -- each up to a stated per-measure Max Rebate amount. Excludes design/planning, permitting, ongoing maintenance beyond the covered annual checkup, and monitoring costs, none of which are listed as eligible.

Covers: a one-year property tax abatement at $10.00/sq ft of green roof (standard), or $15.00/sq ft for properties in designated priority community districts; capped at $200,000 or the property taxes due that year, whichever is lower, with unused amount carried forward up to five years. Excludes: construction/installation costs are not reimbursed directly, and ongoing maintenance is an unfunded applicant obligation.

Covers: up to $2,500 for nonprofit/civic-led small-scale green infrastructure projects (rain gardens, tree planting, rain barrels, other rainwater capture on organizational land), conditioned on holding a volunteer/outreach event before grant close-out; past recipients may also receive supplemental funding for maintenance or advancement of their original project. Excludes: for-profit businesses, schools, and churches applying on their own (only eligible if partnered with a nonprofit); individual homeowners are not eligible for this cash grant (a separate non-monetary "RYR at Home" resource and the Stormwater Fee Reduction Program apply to residents instead); no mention of coverage for design/permitting/monitoring costs.
Physical product and delivery; other costs not stated
Reduces recurring stormwater utility charges for qualifying BMPs; 40% residential credit documented for four barrels; capital, design, permit and maintenance costs not stated as covered

Covers: cash rebate per square foot of grass/turf removed and replaced with qualifying desert/water-smart landscaping (drip irrigation, mulch or permeable surfacing, ≥50% living plant canopy at maturity), plus a $100/tree bonus (Tree Enhancement Program) for qualifying new trees up to 100% canopy coverage. Excludes: project design fees, permit costs, cost of removing existing landscape elements not part of the new design, and non-permeable hardscape (concrete patios, curbing, walkways, driveway extensions) which is subtracted from the incentive area; ongoing maintenance is not covered by the one-time rebate. Artificial turf is permitted only as a mulch substitute (not separately funded), and removal of non-turf plants/high-water-use plants is not covered.
Qualifying barrel purchase price/components; excludes tax, installation and related items
Area-based turf rebate; for device rebates, amount may be limited to qualifying device cost and excludes tax, shipping, labour and other charges.

Covers barrel, tax and home delivery; other costs Not stated

Covers: purchase cost of qualifying equipment/materials (e.g., graywater diverter/valve/PVC conveyance line, irrigation hardware, flowmeters, trees as lawn-conversion add-on, clothes washers) up to per-measure caps, plus free mulch/compost and free indoor water-saving devices, plus a 2-hour professional landscape design consultation ($200 value); Excludes: taxes, labor/installation labor costs, and shipping fees (explicitly excluded for graywater); does not cover ongoing maintenance or monitoring costs; commercial customers additionally get customized equipment rebates and on-bill financing covering upfront capital costs of savings-generating upgrades.

Covers: discounted purchase price ($60, subsidised) of one 50-gallon Ivy rain barrel per verified Ogden household, including all included hardware for self-assembly (6' overflow hose, screen and screen ring, 2 releasable zip ties, overflow cap, 3/4" plastic ball valve). Excludes: professional installation labor (only self-install instructions/videos provided), maintenance/upkeep costs, permitting/registration fees (registering 3+ barrels with Utah Division of Water Rights is a separate user obligation), and any additional barrels beyond the first, which are available only at full price ($88) with no household limit and no subsidy.

Covers 50% match reimbursement of materials, equipment and labor costs for eligible practices: rain gardens, bioswales, and native plant stream buffers (up to $1,000), rain barrels (up to $75 each, limit two per household), and compost bins; limited to one reimbursement per household per calendar year; excludes design/permitting/monitoring costs (not mentioned as covered) and any costs beyond the 50% match or per-item caps; funded practice must be maintained for a minimum of three years, with property access required for rain garden/bioswale/buffer projects before, during, and after construction.

Covers: a rebate toward purchase cost of rain barrel(s), $25 per barrel up to a maximum of 4 per residence ($100 cap); requires dated sales receipt showing item(s) and purchase price; City reserves the right to verify installation (installation itself, i.e. hardware/labor beyond the barrel purchase, is not covered/reimbursed). Excludes: installation labor/materials costs, design/planning, permitting, ongoing maintenance, and monitoring (not mentioned/covered).

Covers water-conservation/efficiency measures only: turf/lawn replacement with water-efficient landscaping at $2/sq ft (Turf Replacement Program), irrigation system upgrades (RISE), and water softener replacement rebates. Excludes (not stated/not documented): design, planning, permitting, maintenance, or monitoring costs, and no NbS-specific measures (green roofs, green façades, rain gardens, rain barrels/cisterns, trees, permeable paving) are named on the programme pages.
Covers purchase of qualifying new rain-barrel or cistern unit; capacity and installation requirements apply; homemade units excluded
Proper installation of eligible rain barrels, rain gardens, native trees and native plants

Covers: discounted barrel unit, filter screen, spigot/tap, flexible downspout connector, overflow hose, linking hose (for 2nd barrel), and free home delivery. Excludes: installation labor/tools (hacksaw, platform materials -- resident-supplied), ongoing maintenance/winterization labor, and any liability for malfunction, property damage or injury (explicitly disclaimed).

Covers, up to stated per-measure caps/rebate amounts: turf-to-desert-landscape conversion ($2/sq ft), rotary nozzle conversion ($4/nozzle, max $2,000), free smart controller purchase+install (and free recycling of old controller), free indoor water conservation kit, ENERGY STAR washing machine purchase (max $150), high-efficiency toilet purchase (max $100) plus toilet-recycling fee ($10), and hot water recirculating pump purchase (max $125 or actual cost, whichever less); discounted (not free) self-install Rachio controller and Flume monitor via partner discount, not a CVWD rebate. Excludes: labor/installation costs beyond the free controller service, design/planning and permitting costs, ongoing maintenance, and monitoring/verification costs; customer must front all purchase costs (reimbursed after proof of purchase) and bears ancillary costs such as the toilet-recycling fee itself (district only rebates $10 of it) and any costs above the stated caps.

Measure-based installation rebates at the current rates above; combined caps $6,000/$135,000; prior approval/Notice to Proceed required. Design, permit, maintenance and monitoring costs are not documented as covered

Covered: turf/grass removal and replacement with desert (xeriscape) landscaping -- plants, drip-irrigation system components (filter, pressure regulator, low-flow emitters), and mulch/permeable surface treatments (rock, bark, permeable pavers, permeable artificial turf); new tree installation is covered via the separate Tree Enhancement Program bonus ($100/tree). Rebate is calculated per converted square foot, tiered ($5/sq ft first 10,000 sq ft, then $1.50-$2.50/sq ft depending on property type), with well-owner rebates capped at 2,500 sq ft/fiscal year subject to special fund availability. Excluded: design fees, permit costs, cost of removing existing landscape elements not part of the new design, and non-permeable hardscape (concrete patios, driveways, walkways, curbing, plastic/impermeable weed barriers) -- these non-permeable areas are explicitly subtracted from the eligible conversion area before the incentive is calculated.

Pays per square foot of qualifying turf replaced; supports required planting, irrigation conversion and onsite rainwater capture. Specific invoices or cost categories do not determine the turf payment
Covers discounted product purchase and scheduled pickup; compost-bin purchase includes scrap bucket; other costs Not stated
City supplies one rain barrel; installation and associated property work are not documented as covered

Measure-specific: barrels; GI construction; drainage repairs; professional design/services up to stated limits; private infrastructure maintenance. Permits and costs beyond approved caps remain applicant responsibilities.
Covers qualifying devices, trees and landscape conversions; excludes taxes, standard installation costs, discounts, artificial turf, high-water-use plants, underlay and water-intensive features

Covers device/rebate costs for: Turf Replacement Program ($6/sq ft total, incl. $3/sq ft optional add-on tree rebate at $100/tree, max 5 trees, tree rebate only with turf rebate), High Efficiency Clothes Washers, Premium High Efficiency Toilets (≤1.06 GPF), Weather-Based Irrigation Controllers, Rotating Sprinkler Nozzles (min qty 30), Soil Moisture Sensor Systems, Rain Barrels (max qty 2), and Cisterns (200-500, 501-999, 1,000+ gallon tiers, amounts not specified on page). Excludes: green roofs/façades, rain gardens/bioswales, permeable paving, and design, permitting, monitoring, and maintenance costs (not mentioned); approval not guaranteed and subject to funding availability/first-come-first-served.
Covers free compost, cardboard, mulch and delivery; qualifying single-family accounts may receive a drip-irrigation conversion kit. Cash reimbursement and installation labour are not stated.

Covers design and construction costs of stormwater retrofit (GSI/SMP) projects on non-residential properties, including required environmental due diligence as part of the application; excludes ongoing O&M costs (owner must submit and separately fund an Operations and Maintenance contract/plan as a condition of the grant, and no such contract may be funded through it) and excludes residential properties (grants program is limited to non-residential properties)

Covers: a cash incentive of $2 per square foot for grass/turf physically removed and replaced with low-water-use, desert-adapted landscaping (minimum 250 sq ft removed, pre-approval/Notice to Proceed required). Excludes: reinstallation of grass on the removal area, leaving bare soil after removal, and installation of water features or pools in the removal area; cost of new plants/materials, design, and permitting/application costs are not identified as reimbursed items.
Qualifying turf conversion area, eligible trees, required planting, stormwater feature and irrigation modification

Covers (via rebates/discounts, free surveys, and free kits): indoor high-efficiency fixtures (showerheads, aerators, toilets, clothes washers); smart/weather-based irrigation controllers (incl. discounted Rachio units), soil moisture sensors, efficient sprinkler nozzles, spray-to-drip irrigation conversion; rain barrels/cisterns; turf-to-drought-tolerant-landscape removal ($3/sq ft, permits may be required); a Flume water-flow monitoring device (discounted, not fully free); free indoor/outdoor water-use surveys and free large-landscape surveys (>1 acre); free indoor conservation kits (max 2/household residential, bulk for multifamily); commercial/institutional rebates for HVAC, medical/dental, food-service, plumbing, and landscape equipment; and customized commercial/industrial/agricultural water-efficiency projects and water-management services under WSIP. Not stated as covered: design/planning costs, permitting fees, ongoing maintenance costs, or monitoring costs beyond the discounted Flume device; nature-based measures such as rain gardens/bioswales, green roofs/façades, permeable paving, and tree planting are not mentioned in any source and are treated as excluded/not offered.
Purchaser pays listed product price; no reimbursement or eligible-cost reimbursement scheme documented
Covers qualifying materials: plants, irrigation equipment, compost and mulch. Excludes sales tax, delivery, rental, installation, labour, personal items and tools
Qualifying turf conversion area, eligible trees and approved water-saving devices; excludes nonqualifying products and homemade barrels/cisterns

Covers: the rain barrel unit itself, flexible downspout connecting elbow, linking/overflow hose, leaf and mosquito filter screen, spigot/tap, printed instructions, and free delivery to the resident's home. Excludes: installation labor (resident self-installs), platform/stand materials (concrete blocks or pressure-treated wood recommended but not supplied), tools required for cutting downspout, ongoing maintenance/winterization supplies, and any repair or replacement beyond manufacturer warranty.
Utility-charge reduction; no installation, permitting or maintenance expenses reimbursed
Covers eligible new rain barrel/cistern purchase. Excludes tax, shipping, labour and other charges. Homemade, used or refurbished equipment is ineligible

Covers: purchase discount and rebate toward cost of a professionally designed low-water perennial garden kit (plants) for residential or business yard, replacing turf lawn. Excludes: hardscape (permeable paving, rain barrels, green roofs), design/permitting/maintenance costs beyond the kit itself, and any support beyond one kit per customer.

Covers: design and construction (hard and soft costs) of green roof retrofits on existing private buildings in NYC -- including required components (root barrier, drainage layer, filter layer, growing media, vegetation) and a required structural analysis; funding rate scaled by soil depth and green roof area (GRA). Excludes: all other green infrastructure measure types (rain gardens, permeable paving, trees, cisterns, etc., not eligible measures under this program) and projects below minimum thresholds (soil depth <1.5in, GRA <3,500 SF, or total project cost <$50,000).
Subsidised rain-barrel unit purchase only; no installation or maintenance benefit is stated

Covers: design and construction/installation costs of approved GSI project types (cistern, downspout disconnection, green roof, impervious surface removal, permeable pavement, rain garden, constructed wetland), reimbursed up to 90% of eligible costs citywide (100% under the Rainwater Rewards Subsidy Program for underserved communities, non-profits, and places of worship), paid after installation via submitted invoices/photos. Excludes: projects done to meet regulatory requirements or for utility fee credits; ongoing maintenance costs are not covered -- applicant bears responsibility for a 5- or 10-year maintenance term and annual maintenance reporting.

Covers: rebates toward the purchase/installation cost of eligible outdoor items (high-efficiency sprinklers at $4/sprinkler, weather-based irrigation controllers at $150 each, drought-tolerant plant conversions at $1/sq ft up to $1,000, irrigation-less groundcover conversions at $1/sq ft up to $1,000, small grove irrigation retrofits at $1/150 gallons saved/year, and other qualifying water-conserving products) and indoor items (high-efficiency toilets at $100 each, high-efficiency washing machines at $200 each); free pre-inspection, post-inspection, and water-use audits are included. Excludes: any rebate amount exceeding the purchase price of the product; costs of design/planning, permitting, labor beyond the qualifying inspections, ongoing maintenance/monitoring; non-permeable/prohibited materials (e.g., plastic or non-permeable weed barriers, solid concrete); and any work performed before the required pre-inspection. Combined rebates across all incentive items are capped at $1,000 per customer per fiscal year, except Small Grove Irrigation Retrofit, which is exempt from the $1,000 cap (subject to its own limited funding).
Covers qualifying rain-barrel/cistern purchase and installation; excludes sales tax from rebate calculation

Covers: purchase and installation cost (itemized receipt required, purchase and installation must be listed separately) of qualifying high-efficiency toilets (up to $50/unit, max 2), high-efficiency washing machines ($100, max 1), weather-based smart irrigation timers ($100, max 1), high-efficiency/automatic shut-off irrigation nozzles ($4/$10 per nozzle, no limit), and turf removal/water-efficient landscaping ($1/sq ft, max $1,000). Excludes: any amount exceeding the fixed per-measure rebate caps and never exceeding the purchase price; non-qualifying/non-listed products; concrete as a turf-replacement material; and implicitly design/permitting, ongoing maintenance/monitoring costs (not listed as reimbursable items, only purchase+installation is referenced); customer must self-fund upfront and comply with local landscape ordinances as a condition of the turf rebate.
Stormwater utility fee reduction only; installation and ongoing maintenance costs remain with the property owner/applicant
Subsidised purchase price of rain barrels/accessories (and compost bins in the broader sale); no installation or maintenance reimbursement stated

Covers: (1) High-efficiency rotating sprinkler nozzle replacements at $2.00/nozzle for qualifying products; (2) EPA WaterSense smart irrigation controller replacements (of old timers) at up to $300 rebate for qualifying products; (3) Xeriscaping turf removal at $1.00/sq ft of real grass turf removed, requiring pre-approval before starting the project and a minimum 250 sq ft of real grass turf in place at pre-approval. Qualifying new rain-barrel or cistern equipment purchase at the published rates; additional component restrictions are governed by SoCal WaterSmart

Covers: the physical rain barrel unit, flexible connecting elbow/downspout connector, leaf and mosquito filter screen, spigot/tap, overflow hose, linking hose for a second barrel, delivery to home, and printed/video installation instructions. Covers: reimbursement of rain barrel purchase/installation at $0.75/gallon of storage capacity, capped at $150, for above-ground barrels connected to a gutter downspout that meet siting/use conditions (solid level foundation; covered against mosquitoes/rodents/debris; positioned to receive gutter water unimpeded; clear of walkways; used for landscape irrigation). Covers: reduction of billed impervious area (stormwater fee credit) for rain barrels, rain gardens, cisterns, and drywells; subsidised purchase price for city-sold rain barrels. Rebate of $1/gallon for at least 500 gallons; $500 minimum and $2,000 maximum. Applicant bears CSI, possible backflow and permit costs. Potable backup and properties with irrigation systems are ineligible.

Partial reimbursement for approved landscape conversion, pool conversion, lawn-to-mulch projects, in-line drip conversion, qualifying irrigation equipment and rainwater-capture installations; prior purchases/work are ineligible; total payments are subject to lifetime caps and available funding
Rebate limited to documented eligible materials/equipment and applicable caps; taxes and labour are excluded from several equipment rebates

Covers/subsidises the barrel purchase price; transport/storage savings embedded; installation and accessories not stated as covered

Rebates cover purchase price of qualifying equipment up to stated maximums. Rain barrels: size-based rebate ($12-$50). Cisterns: per-gallon rebate with bonus options. Irrigation equipment and indoor appliances: fixed amounts. Retrofit only, not for new construction. Original receipts required.

Covers a portion of pre-approved design, water-wise plants, smart irrigation systems and landscape materials, up to the applicable project cap; excludes new-construction landscapes and retroactive projects; sale receipts or contractor invoices are required

Covers: rebate payment for removal of living turf grass and installation of climate-appropriate/California-inspired landscaping (Cash for Grass); rebate for converting operational spray sprinklers in planter beds/hedges to drip irrigation (Spray to Drip). 90-100% of total installation cost; specified extras may remain out-of-pocket

Covers: cost of water-wise/drought-tolerant plants purchased (up to $300); curbing/metal edging materials or installation (up to $250); hardscape materials such as concrete, pavers, decks, patios (up to $500/yr, $1/sqft); free landscaping rock, weed barrier, and drip system conversion kit materials (in-kind) for park strip conversions. Covers: purchase and installation cost of qualifying rain barrels/cisterns (rebate up to $200 or actual cost, whichever is less, excluding sales tax); and turf/lawn removal and replacement with drought-tolerant landscaping (rebate up to $4/sq.ft.), plus an optional additional Rain Garden rebate ($300) if added to a Lawn Be Gone! project. Covers: cost of the rain barrel unit, leaf/mosquito filter screen, spigot/tap, flexible downspout connector, overflow hose, linking hose for a second barrel, and free delivery. Covers 50% of purchase cost and/or installation of rain barrels, drip irrigation, native plants (from approved list), smart water controllers, and rain sensors, up to a lifetime cumulative cap of $150 per resident/water customer (rain sensors sub-capped at $80 rebate on a $160 purchase); does not cover ongoing maintenance, monitoring, design/planning, or permitting, and no other landscape features (e.g., green roofs, rain gardens, permeable paving, trees) are listed as eligible

Covers: cost of low-water plants/landscape conversion ($1-2/sq.ft.), WaterSense irrigation controllers (up to $200), rain sensors (up to $25), WaterSense toilet replacement (up to $75/unit, existing installed toilets only, not new construction), lawn removal service (city covers $1.75/sq.ft. up to $750) and discounted Garden in a Box kits.
